title: Bunkhouse Hotels Launches "Vote Y'all" Campaign to Encourage Voter Registration
summary: [Chicago, IL – August 10, 2026] – Bunkhouse Hotels has announced the launch of Vote Y'all, a civic engagement campaign encouraging Texans to register to vote ahead of the October 2026 voter...
body_text: [Chicago, IL – August 11, 2026] – Bunkhouse Hotels has announced the launch of Vote Y'all , a civic engagement campaign encouraging Texans to register to vote ahead of the October 2026 voter registration deadline. Beginning in August, the initiative will bring voter registration opportunities to Austin Motel and Carpenter Hotel, alongside a social media campaign across Bunkhouse Hotels’ channels, limited edition “Vote Y’all” retail benefitting MOVE Texas ’s voter registration work, and three "Vote Y'all" billboards throughout Austin to inspire civic participation. Bunkhouse Hotels have long created gathering places that serve both travelers and the communities surrounding its properties. Vote Y’all builds upon that commitment by making voter registration available in an approachable, welcoming, and familiar neighborhood setting. The campaign is presented in collaboration with MOVE Texas, a nonpartisan nonprofit organization dedicated to bringing Texans together and encouraging them to register to vote leading up to the general election. "We're thrilled to welcome MOVE Texas back to Bunkhouse Hotels and give our community a welcoming place to register to vote at Austin Motel and Carpenter Hotel," said Erin Lindsey, Regional Vice President of Brand & Marketing, Bunkhouse Hotels & JdV by Hyatt. "We've loved collaborating with MOVE at events over the years, most recently at our 19th Annual Chili Cook-Off, so teaming up again this fall felt like an easy yes." On Saturdays throughout August and September, guests and community members can visit Austin Motel and Carpenter Hotel between noon and 4:00 p.m. to register to vote. Custom Vote Y’all retail items including t-shirts, totes, and more will also be available for purchase. Bunkhouse Hotels will donate to MOVE Texas’s voter registration efforts 25% of the price of participating sold from August 8, 2026, until December 31, 2026, while supplies last. Vote Y'all Voter Registration Events Austin Motel Saturdays | 12:00 p.m. – 4:00 p.m. August 8 August 15 August 22 August 29 Carpenter Hotel Saturdays | 12:00 p.m. – 4:00 p.m. September 5 September 12 September 19 September 26 ABOUT BUNKHOUSE HOTELS With a passion for design, a commitment to community, and tireless attention to detail, Bunkhouse Hotels create soulful travel experiences for guests and locals that are authentically grounded in a sense of place. Enjoy World of Hyatt benefits with eligible stays at participating Bunkhouse Hotels – discover more here . ABOUT MOVE TEXAS MOVE Texas (Mobilize. Organize. Vote. Empower.) is a nonpartisan, nonprofit organization dedicated to building the political power of young people in underrepresented communities through civic engagement, leadership development, and issue advocacy. Its vision is to build the political power of young people to transform democracy in Texas and beyond. Learn more here . ABOUT HYATT HOTELS CORPORATION Hyatt Hotels Corporation, headquartered in Chicago, is a leading global hospitality company guided by its purpose – to care for people so they can be their best. As of March 31, 2026, the Company's portfolio included more than 1,500 hotels and all-inclusive properties in 83 countries across six continents. The Company's offering includes brands in the Luxury Portfolio , including Park Hyatt ®, Alila ®, Miraval ®, Impression by Secrets , and The Unbound Collection by Hyatt ®; the Lifestyle Portfolio , including Andaz ®, Thompson Hotels ®, The Standard ®, Dream ® Hotels , The StandardX ®, Breathless Resorts & Spas ®, JdV by Hyatt ®, Bunkhouse ® Hotels , and Me and All Hotels ; the Inclusive Collection , including Zoëtry ® Wellness & Spa Resorts , Hyatt Ziva ®, Hyatt Zilara ®, Secrets ® Resorts & Spas , Dreams ® Resorts & Spas , Hyatt Vivid ® Hotels & Resorts , Bahia Principe Hotels & Resorts, Alua Hotels & Resorts ®, and Sunscape ® Resorts & Spas ; the Classics Portfolio , including Grand Hyatt ®, Hyatt Regency ®, Destination by Hyatt ®, Hyatt Centric ®, Hyatt Vacation Club ®, and Hyatt ®; and the Essentials Portfolio , including Caption by Hyatt ®, Unscripted by Hyatt , Hyatt Place ®, Hyatt House ®, Hyatt Studios ®, Hyatt Select, and UrCove . title: Best Body Wash for Sensitive Skin: Dermatologist Recommended Picks
summary: Struggling with dry, itchy or irritated skin after bathing? Find the best body wash for sensitive skin, key ingredients to look for & what to avoid.
body_text: Sensitive Skin Ingredients for Sensitive Skin Ingredients to Avoid Top Body Washes for Sensitive Skin Choosing Body Washes for Sensitive Skin FAQs Sensitive skin can react quickly to everyday products. A body wash that feels comfortable for one person may cause another to experience dryness, tightness, itching, redness, or stinging. Choosing a cleanser based on your skin's needs is especially important if your skin is already dry or easily irritated. A suitable body wash for sensitive skin should remove sweat, dirt, and excess oil without leaving the skin feeling excessively dry or tight. Soap-free and mild cleansing formulas may be preferable for people who experience dryness or irritation after bathing. Ingredients such as colloidal oatmeal, glycerin, panthenol, and hyaluronic acid can also help support skin hydration and comfort. In this blog, we will discuss how to choose the best body wash for sensitive skin, which ingredients to look for, which ones may cause irritation, and some suitable options to consider. What Is Sensitive Skin? Sensitive skin refers to skin that reacts more easily to external triggers such as skincare products, weather changes, heat, friction, or certain ingredients. People with sensitive skin may experience symptoms such as redness, itching, burning, stinging, or discomfort after exposure to triggers that do not bother other people. The outermost layer of the skin, called the stratum corneum, forms an important part of the skin barrier. This skin barrier helps reduce water loss while protecting against external irritants and microorganisms. Changes in skin-barrier function can contribute to increased sensitivity, although sensitive skin can also involve an increased response to external stimuli. This can make the skin feel uncomfortable or reactive during everyday activities such as bathing, particularly when exposed to hot water, frequent washing, or irritating products. Signs Your Skin May Be Sensitive Sensitive skin can affect people differently. Some may notice occasional discomfort after using certain products, while others may experience repeated redness, itching, or stinging. These symptoms can also occur with conditions such as eczema or contact dermatitis, so they do not necessarily mean that you have sensitive skin. Common signs may include: Redness and Flushing: Your skin may become red or feel uncomfortable after exposure to heat, sunlight, friction, or certain skincare products. Dryness and Tightness: Your skin may feel dry, tight, rough, or uncomfortable, particularly after bathing or cleansing. Itching and Stinging: You may notice itching, burning, or stinging after using certain soaps, body washes, or skincare products. Dryness and Flaking: The skin may become rough, flaky, or scaly, especially when it is dry or irritated. Reactivity to Products: Certain ingredients, including fragrances or preservatives, may trigger redness, itching, burning, or other signs of irritation. If these symptoms occur frequently or persist despite using gentle skincare, consult a dermatologist to determine whether an underlying skin condition may be contributing to them. Why Does Sensitive Skin Need a Different Body Wash? Cleansing helps remove sweat, dirt, excess oil, and other substances from the skin, but frequent washing or harsh cleansing can also remove some of the skin's natural lipids. Hot water and prolonged bathing may further increase dryness and discomfort. For sensitive skin, choosing a mild cleanser can help reduce unnecessary stress on the skin during bathing. When choosing a body wash for sensitive skin, look for a formula that: Helps Maintain Moisture: Cleanses the skin without leaving it feeling excessively dry or tight after bathing. Uses Mild Cleansing Agents: Removes sweat, dirt, and excess oil while avoiding an overly harsh cleansing experience. Supports Skin Hydation: Ingredients such as glycerin, panthenol, or colloidal oatmeal can help support skin hydration and comfort. Has a Skin-Friendly pH: A mildly acidic formula can help support the skin's normal barrier environment during cleansing. Ingredients That Can Help Sensitive Skin When choosing a body wash for sensitive skin, checking the ingredient list can help you identify formulas designed to support hydration and skin comfort. No single ingredient works for everyone, but certain moisturizing and skin-conditioning ingredients are commonly used in products for dry or sensitive skin. Some ingredients to look for include: Colloidal Oatmeal : It may soothe dry, itchy skin and support the skin barrier. Glycerin: It helps attract and retain water in the outer layer of skin, supporting hydration. Panthenol (Pro-Vitamin B5): This hydrates and conditions skin, leaving it soft and comfortable. Ceramides: They support the skin barrier and help reduce moisture loss. Their benefits are generally better established in leave-on skincare than in rinse-off cleansers. Hyaluronic Acid: It attracts water to support hydration, though benefits may be limited in rinse-off products. Niacinamide (Vitamin B3): This supports the skin barrier and hydration in well-formulated products. Aloe Vera: This may moisturize and help soothe dry or irritated skin. Ingredients That May Irritate Sensitive Skin Some ingredients or cleansing formulas may cause dryness or irritation, particularly when the skin is already dry or reactive. It is also important to understand the broader do’s and don'ts of skincare for sensitive skin , as everyday products and habits can contribute to irritation. Instead of avoiding broad ingredient categories automatically, pay attention to products that consistently cause discomfort and identify any personal triggers. Ingredients or formulations that may be worth limiting include: Fragrance: It may cause irritation or allergic contact dermatitis in some people. Fragrance-free products may be preferable if you are sensitive to fragrance. Harsh Cleansing Formulas: Strongly degreasing cleansers may increase dryness or irritation, especially with frequent use. High Concentration of Drying Alcohols: High levels of volatile alcohols may be drying or irritating. Exfoliants: Acids and scrubs can increase irritation if overused or on already sensitive skin. Personal Triggers: Avoid any ingredient that has previously caused a reaction. Best Body Washes for Sensitive Skin Choosing a body wash for sensitive skin depends on factors such as dryness, ingredient sensitivity, and how your skin feels after cleansing. A formula that works well for one person may not suit another, so consider the product's ingredients and your specific skin needs when making a choice. Here are some body washes that may be suitable for sensitive skin: Product Key Ingredients Benefits Aquaderm Face & Body Wash Hyaluronic Acid, Cocamidopropyl Betaine Gently cleanses while supporting skin hydration. Aveeno Skin Relief Body Wash Colloidal Oatmeal, Glycerin Cleanses and helps soothe very dry, sensitive skin. Moisturex Wash Body Wash Glycerin, Calendula Extract Cleanses while helping maintain skin moisture and softness. BABE Hydra-Calm Body Wash Aloe Vera, Chamomile Provides gentle cleansing with soothing and moisturizing benefits. FCL Oatsilk Soap Free Body Wash Cocamidopropyl Betaine, Aloe Leaf Juice Provides soap-free cleansing while supporting hydration and skin comfort. Numis Med pH 5.5 Face & Body Wash for Very Sensitive Skin Panthenol, Hydrolactol Provides gentle cleansing while supporting the skin's natural pH environment. 1. Aquaderm Face & Body Wash Aquaderm Face & Body Wash is a soap-free cleanser for people with sensitive skin who want a mild option for everyday cleansing. It can be used on both the face and body, making it a convenient choice for a simple cleansing routine. Here’s why it stands out: Soap-Free Cleansing: It offers an alternative to conventional soap-based cleansers. Supports Skin Hydration: Its formulation includes hyaluronic acid, which can help support skin hydration. Face and Body Use: It can be used as part of a daily cleansing routine for both the face and body. 2. Aveeno Skin Relief Body Wash Aveeno Skin Relief Body Wash is formulated for dry, itchy, and sensitive skin. It combines colloidal oatmeal with emollients and gentle cleansers to help cleanse the skin while supporting moisture and comfort. The fragrance-free formula is also soap-free and dye-free, making it a suitable option for people who prefer to avoid added fragrance in their body care routine. Colloidal Oatmeal: Contains colloidal oatmeal, an ingredient commonly used to soothe and moisturize dry, sensitive skin. Fragrance-Free Formula: Contains no added fragrance, which may be preferable for people whose skin is easily irritated by fragrance. Soap and Dye Free: The formula is free from soap and dyes for a simpler cleansing option for sensitive skin. 3. Moisturex Wash Body Wash Moisturex Wash Body Wash is a soap-free cleanser designed for sensitive skin and everyday bathing. It provides a milder alternative to conventional soap while helping cleanse the skin without stripping its natural oils. Let’s understand why it stands out: Soap-Free Formula: It provides an alternative to traditional soap-based cleansing for people looking for a milder body wash. Helps Maintain Skin Moisture: Glycerin helps support hydration and a comfortable skin feel after washing. Soothing Ingredients: Green tea and calendula extracts are included to help support skin comfort during cleansing. 4. BABE Hydra-Calm Body Wash BABE Hydra-Calm Body Wash is a cleansing gel formulated for sensitive and dry skin. Its syndet-based formula is designed for gentle daily cleansing, while ingredients such as aloe vera, chamomile, allantoin, and jojoba help support skin comfort and hydration. Its key features are: Syndet Formula: Uses a soap-free cleansing base designed for sensitive and dry skin. Soothing Ingredients: Contains aloe vera, chamomile, and allantoin to help support skin comfort during cleansing. Daily Use: It can be used regularly as part of a shower or bath routine. 5. FCL Oatsilk Soap Free Body Wash FCL Oatsilk Soap Free Body Wash is formulated for sensitive skin and provides a soap-free approach to everyday cleansing. Its formula contains colloidal oatmeal, linoleic acid, and sodium PCA, along with a pH-balanced cleansing base designed to support skin comfort. Here’s what makes it stand out: pH-Balanced Formula: Its mildly acidic formulation is designed to support the skin's natural protective environment. Colloidal Oatmeal: Contains colloidal oatmeal, which can help soothe dry and itchy skin and support skin hydration. Soap-Free Cleansing: Provides an alternative to conventional soap-based cleansers for people with sensitive or dry skin. 6. Numis Med pH 5.5 Face & Body Wash For Very Sensitive Skin Numis Med pH 5.5 Face & Body Wash is formulated for very sensitive skin and can be used on both the face and body. Its pH 5.5 formulation is designed to support the skin's natural acidic environment during cleansing, making it an option for people looking for a mild, pH-focused cleanser. Some of its key features are: pH 5.5 Formulation: Its mildly acidic pH is designed to support the skin's natural pH environment. Face and Body Use: It can be used to cleanse both the face and body as part of a regular bathing routine. Gentle Cleansing: It is formulated for very sensitive skin and is intended for daily cleansing without excessive dryness or discomfort. How to Choose the Best Body Wash for Sensitive Skin The right body wash can make bathing more comfortable when your skin is easily irritated. Instead of choosing a product based only on its claims, consider its ingredients, cleansing formula, and how your skin responds after use. Here is what to look for: Choose Mild Formulas: Look for cleansers that do not leave skin dry or tight. Prefer Fragrance-Free: Fragrance may irritate sensitive skin. Look for Moisturizing Ingredients: Glycerin, colloidal oatmeal, and panthenol support hydration. Consider Your Skin's Needs: Choose formulas based on dryness, itching, or irritation. Check the pH: A mildly acidic pH supports the skin's natural environment. Use Lukewarm Water: Avoid hot water and keep showers short. Wash Gently: Avoid scrubbing with rough washcloths, loofahs, or sponges. Moisturize After Bathing: Apply moisturizer while skin is slightly damp. Stop if Irritation Develops: Discontinue products that cause persistent burning, itching, or redness. When Should You See a Dermatologist? Sensitive skin can often be managed with a gentle cleansing and moisturizing routine. However, persistent or recurring symptoms may have an underlying cause that needs medical evaluation. Consider seeing a dermatologist if you notice: Persistent Redness or Itching: Symptoms that do not improve with gentle skincare. Recurring Rashes: Repeated or unexplained reactions after using skincare products. Severe Dryness or Cracking: Painful, cracked, or bleeding skin that does not improve. Blisters or Swelling: Blistering, significant swelling, oozing, or crusting. Worsening Symptoms: A rash that spreads quickly, becomes painful, or shows signs of infection. Conditions such as eczema or contact dermatitis can cause symptoms similar to sensitive skin. If a body wash causes a reaction, stop using it and consult a dermatologist if the symptoms persist or are severe. Final Thoughts Choosing the best body wash for sensitive skin is about finding a cleanser that removes dirt and sweat without leaving the skin feeling excessively dry, tight, or irritated. Mild, fragrance-free formulas with moisturizing ingredients can be a good starting point for sensitive skin. Use lukewarm water, avoid vigorous scrubbing, and moisturize soon after bathing to help maintain skin comfort and hydration. If your skin continues to itch, burn, develop rashes, or react despite using gentle products, consult a dermatologist for appropriate evaluation.

title: 15 Best Business Development Tools to Grow Pipeline in 2026
summary: Explore the top tools for prospecting, CRM, outreach, enrichment, automation, and revenue workflows, plus how to choose the right stack.
body_text: Business development teams need more than a CRM to grow pipeline in 2026. They need tools that help them find the right accounts, manage outreach, enrich lead data, automate follow-up, track opportunities, and keep every revenue workflow connected. This guide compares 15 of the best business development tools for CRM, prospecting, outreach, data enrichment, automation, and sales workflows. You’ll see what each tool is best for, how it fits into a growth stack, and what to consider before adding another platform to your team’s workflow. The goal is not to collect more software. It is to build a business development system that helps your team move faster, follow up consistently, and turn more opportunities into revenue. What are business development tools? Definition and scope Business development tools are software products that help companies identify opportunities, open new markets, win customers, and expand accounts. This stack typically spans prospecting and CRM, sales engagement and marketing automation, data and analytics, partner and customer portals, and the low code or no code platforms used to build custom workflows and apps. In practical terms, business development tools unify four motions that often operate separately, demand generation, sales execution, account growth, and product led expansion. When connected, these tools create a feedback loop where insights from one motion improve the others. Why business development tools matter for growth Three forces make business development tools essential for growth. Buyers expect connected experiences. CRM and marketing software investment keeps rising, with CRM marketing projected to reach about 46 billion dollars by 2028. ( gartner.com ) AI is changing digital buying behavior. AI influenced online holiday sales reached 229 billion dollars globally in 2024, and chatbot usage rose 42 percent year over year, which pressures teams to modernize discovery and support flows. ( reuters.com ) The API first shift speeds integration. Eighty two percent of organizations practice some level of API first and about 65 percent generate revenue from APIs, which makes integration strategy central to revenue strategy. ( postman.com ) Core types of business development tools CRM and customer data platforms, manage contacts, opportunities, and revenue forecasting Sales engagement and enablement, orchestrate sequences, call coaching, and buyer collaboration Marketing automation and advertising, run campaigns, lead capture, and lead scoring Data enrichment and intent, improve lead quality and account intelligence Analytics and forecasting, visualize pipeline health and financial impact Integration and workflow automation, connect apps and sync data across systems Low code and no code app builders, create custom portals, pricing tools, and internal apps that fill process gaps Partner and customer success, manage channel programs and customer lifecycle Key features to look for Open integration approach. Favor platforms that connect to any API , publish webhooks, and support iPaaS connectors. The iPaaS market grew 23.4 percent to 8.5 billion dollars in 2024, which shows how central integration has become. ( gartner.com ) Clear data ownership. Teams increasingly require code export, self hosting, and compliance options such as SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR to meet enterprise standards without slowing delivery. Visual builders that export a Vue app and allow on premise deployment give that flexibility. AI that is editable. AI should generate building blocks that humans can refine in a visual editor, rather than lock you into a black box Speed and autonomy. Tools should let cross functional teams prototype and ship without waiting on long release cycles Governance. Look for role based access, environments, audit trails, and design systems to keep quality high at scale Real world proof. Ask for case studies that measure time to value. For instance, one consulting firm cut typical app cycles from years to 4 to 8 weeks using a visual development approach. Trends in business development software for 2026 AI becomes table stakes across the funnel. CRM sales software growth is tied to AI enabled seller efficiency, with the segment reaching 25.7 billion dollars in 2024. ( gartner.com ) API first fuels faster go to market. Fifty seven percent of teams spend at least ten hours per week on API work, and 63 percent can ship an API in under a week, which reduces integration lead times that used to stall deals. ( postman.com ) Low code and no code go enterprise. Low code application platforms are forecast to hit about 16.5 billion dollars by 2027, and buyers expect composable architectures and generative AI. ( gartner.com ) Marketing and lifecycle automation keep expanding. CRM marketing software is on a double digit growth path this decade, driven by personalization and cross channel orchestration. ( gartner.com ) Digital commerce raises the bar for customer experience. During the 2024 season, US online sales rose to about 282 billion dollars and mobile dominated share, while AI assistant traffic on Black Friday 2025 surged several times year over year. That buyer behavior now shapes B2B expectations too. ( reuters.com ) Methodology, why trust this guide and how we selected tools Selection combined market data, independent research, and hands on evaluation. Market signals. We referenced analyst data on CRM, marketing, iPaaS, and low code growth to confirm category importance and momentum. Outcomes that matter. We prioritized products with evidence of revenue impact, faster deployment, or measurable productivity improvements, such as the ability to export and self host code, or documented cycle time reductions. Breadth and fit. Since business development tools serve startups, agencies, and enterprise teams, we looked for flexibility across use cases, including customer portals, internal tools , and full SaaS products Real world adoption. We weighed platforms with visible customer proof, including global brands that require security and compliance, and the ability to deploy on private infrastructure when needed. Which business development tools do you need? The right business development stack depends on the problem you are trying to solve. Before comparing individual platforms, start with the workflow you want to improve: If you need to manage leads and opportunities, start with a CRM. Tools like Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho CRM, monday CRM, and Creatio help teams track contacts, deals, activities, and forecasts. If you need more qualified prospects, add data enrichment or intent tools. Platforms like ZoomInfo, Apollo, Clearbit, Demandbase, and Cognism help teams find better-fit accounts, enrich records, and prioritize outreach. If you need to run outbound campaigns, use sales engagement tools. Tools like LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Outreach, Salesloft, Apollo, and HubSpot Sales Hub help teams build lists, run sequences, manage calls, and follow up consistently. If you need to automate handoffs and internal workflows, look for automation and integration capabilities. This is where teams often need to connect CRM data, lead routing, approvals, reporting, and customer-facing experiences. If your workflow is unique to your business, consider building it in WeWeb. You can create internal tools, dashboards, portals, and workflow apps that connect to your existing systems, without waiting for every change to go through engineering. Build the workflow your stack is missing . Top 15 Business Development Tools Building on the strategy above, this section spotlights the essential platforms teams use to find the right accounts, engage decisively, and keep deals progressing. They’re grouped here because together they cover the full business-development workflow: data enrichment, prospecting, multichannel outreach, and CRM, so you can see how each piece complements the others. title: Lidl Just Overtook Morrisons. Here Is What That Means for Suppliers
summary: Lidl is now Britain's fifth largest supermarket with 50+ new stores planned. Here is what its growth means for UK and Irish suppliers and how to get ready.
body_text: In this article, learn about: Why Lidl becoming Britain's 5th largest supermarket changes the trading landscape for suppliers How Lidl's lean model makes it different to trade with compared to traditional grocers What Lidl requires from suppliers across logistics, quality, and compliance When EDI capability becomes the difference between a smooth Lidl onboarding and a slow one Britain's Fastest-Growing Bricks-and-Mortar Retailer Lidl has overtaken Morrisons to become Britain's 5th largest supermarket. Its market share reached 8.7% in June 2026 , up from 8.1% a year earlier, and more than 3 in 5 UK households now shop there each week. For 35 consecutive months, Lidl GB has held the title of Britain's fastest-growing bricks-and-mortar retailer. Lidl GB at a glance: Market share 8.7% (June 2026) UK ranking Britain's 5th largest supermarket Stores 1,000+ across England, Scotland and Wales Distribution centres 13 New stores planned 50+ in the next 12 months Investment committed £600 million British suppliers Two-thirds of its range In April 2026, Lidl announced it would open more than 50 new stores in the next 12 months, backed by £600 million in investment. A new distribution centre in Leeds will be operational in 2027, extending its northern reach. Already, two-thirds of Lidl's range comes from British suppliers. "Our expansion translates directly into high-quality jobs and gives British suppliers the certainty they need to invest in the future." — Ryan McDonnell, CEO, Lidl GB The opportunity for UK and Irish suppliers is real and growing. So are the requirements. Why Trading with Lidl Is Different Lidl operates a lean, efficient retail model, and every part of the supplier relationship is built to support it. Traditional grocery accounts give suppliers room for incremental process improvement over time. Lidl expects operational readiness from day one. The buying team evaluates suppliers across 4 areas: supply reliability, logistics capability, product quality, and price competitiveness. Each carries equal weight, and a gap in any one of them can stall or end the commercial relationship. That lean model also shapes what a listing is worth. Lidl stores carry a limited, curated range compared to a traditional supermarket, which makes getting on the range more competitive. Suppliers who do secure a listing tend to see higher volume per SKU as a result. What Lidl Requires From Suppliers Logistics Deliveries must arrive on Euro pallets (1,200mm x 800mm) or half pallets (600mm x 800mm), using 1 of 3 approved pallet types: Chep, LPR, or standard stamped Euro pallets. Shrink-wrapped outer cases are not accepted. Products must be shelf-ready and fully shoppable on arrival at the distribution centre. All warehouse deliveries are booked through Lidl's online TSM (Time Slot Management) system, which suppliers are expected to use consistently. Quality Lidl requires a minimum of 75% remaining shelf life at the point of manufacture. Unannounced audits are part of the relationship from the start, and biannual testing continues throughout the listing period. Suppliers are expected to adhere to UK government salt, sugar, and calorie reduction programmes. Listing Types There are 3 routes to getting your products on Lidl shelves: Permanent listings are year-round placements decided at the annual range review. These require ongoing price commitments and shelf-ready, mixed-case packaging. Seasonal listings cover key trading periods, Christmas, Easter, summer, and winter, and suit products with strong seasonal relevance. Food Specials are one-week promotional placements. Suppliers engage with the Food Specials team 10 to 13 weeks in advance and confirm they can fulfil the agreed volume in full 1 to 2 weeks before the promotion goes live. EDI and Compliance Lidl uses EDIFACT for electronic document exchange, transmitted via a Value Added Network (VAN). The 4 core messages suppliers need to support are: Message Purpose ORDERS Purchase orders sent from Lidl to you ORDRSP Your confirmation response to each order DESADV Dispatch advice sent when goods leave your site INVOIC Invoice submission EDI invoicing is not formally mandated, but it is Lidl's preferred approach. Suppliers without it in place before their 1st transaction carry significantly more manual overhead, and retrofitting EDI mid-relationship is harder than getting it right at the start. Having it ready before onboarding begins puts you in a stronger position from day one. SPS Commerce supports suppliers in connecting to Lidl GB via EDI, with pre-built specs already in the network. For a full walkthrough of the Lidl GB onboarding process, this guide covers everything from first contact through to ongoing monitoring. On the compliance side, Lidl operates under the Groceries Supply Code of Practice (GSCOP) , incorporated into all supply agreements and enforced by the Groceries Code Adjudicator. Social compliance requirements include engagement with Sedex and visible, in-date ethical audits for high-risk production sites. The Opportunity Ahead Lidl's growth is not slowing. 50+ stores in the next 12 months means more shelf space, more listing slots, and rising demand from a retailer that already sources two-thirds of its range from British suppliers. As the store count grows, that sourcing needs to grow with it. For suppliers already trading with traditional grocers, adding Lidl as an account takes some adjustment. Logistics requirements are specific, quality standards are tested from day one, and getting EDI right before onboarding avoids friction later. SPS Commerce connects suppliers to Lidl GB and major UK and Irish retailers through a managed trading partner network, with spec knowledge, EDI connections, and compliance monitoring already built in. When Lidl's requirements change, the network updates centrally rather than landing as a change request on your internal team. title: The Data Room CLI: A Live, Permissioned Data Room from Your Terminal
summary: Two commands turn a local folder tree into a live, permissioned data room. The full command reference, the scoped-key auth model, and the honest limits.
body_text: Two commands take a local folder tree to a live, permissioned data room: npx @magelegal/cli login npx @magelegal/cli upload ./diligence The first opens a browser, asks you to confirm a short code, and binds this machine to a room. The second mirrors the folder into the room, in parallel, with processing starting as each document arrives. Node.js 20 or newer is the only prerequisite, and npx means nothing gets installed. That is the whole pitch. The rest of this page is the reference: what each command does, how the credential works, what breaks, and what the tool deliberately will not do. Why run a data room from a terminal at all? Because the documents are already in a folder tree, and the browser is the worst possible way to move 4,000 of them. Three situations make this concrete. A founder assembling a fundraising room has everything in one directory that mirrors how the company actually files things. An associate prepping a sell-side room has an export from the client's file server. A platform team wants the room populated by the same CI job that assembles the closing binder, with no human in the loop. All three want the same thing: local structure in, room structure out, no drag-and-drop marathon, and no shared login pasted into a Slack thread. Install and first run node --version # must be 20 or newer npx @magelegal/cli login Or install it once and drop the npx : npm install -g @magelegal/cli mage --help The package is @magelegal/cli , the executable is mage , it is MIT licensed, and the source is public at github.com/magelegal/mage-dataroom-cli. Runtime dependencies are two small libraries. Cite the install command rather than a version number; the published version moves. login does four things: opens a browser page for your approval, resolves which room this machine should bind to (asking if your organization has several, and offering to create one if the account is brand new), mints a room-scoped API key labelled with this machine's hostname, and stores it locally. On a machine with no browser, or over SSH, pass --no-browser and it prints the approval URL instead. Two constraints before you try. Minting a key requires owner or admin rights on the room. And the login does not expire: it works until the key is revoked. How does the credential actually work? Security is the first objection anyone sensible raises about a CLI that touches deal documents, so here is the model in full. The key the CLI mints for itself is room-scoped . It acts in exactly one room and carries the permission set chosen at mint time, visible under Settings and API keys alongside who minted it and when. A login-minted key can read the room's document list, upload, manage folders, delete documents, download document files, and read and fill the readiness checklist. What it cannot do is the more useful half: It cannot reach another room. It cannot delete the room itself. It cannot change room settings, people, or sharing. That needs the Manage room permission, which is not granted by default. It cannot fetch document contents without the Download permission. Reading the document list and reading the bytes are separate grants. Permissions are immutable after mint. Widening a key means minting a new one, which is the right trade: a key's authority never quietly grows. Revoking a key under Settings and API keys kills it everywhere, instantly. The secret itself is returned exactly once, at creation, and is never recoverable afterward; the room's settings list shows only the room binding, who minted it, its permission set, and its audit trail. Locally, credentials live in ~/.config/mage/config.json at mode 0600, readable only by you. Only two commands act as you rather than as the key: mage rooms and mage use . Everything else runs with the key's authority, which is why a stolen laptop is a revocation problem rather than an account problem. The command reference Command What it does mage login [key] [--room <room>] [--with-key] [--no-browser] Sign in via browser, or store an API key, and bind this machine to a room mage logout Revoke the CLI's key where possible and clear this machine mage rooms List your organization's data rooms (browser login only) mage use <room> Switch which room this machine is bound to (browser login only) mage upload <paths...> [--to <folder>] [--for-item <itemId>] Upload files or whole folders, mirroring their structure mage readiness Show the room's readiness checklist: present, partial, and missing mage readiness attach <itemId> <documents...> Attach already-uploaded documents to a checklist item mage ls [folder] List the room's documents, grouped by folder mage download [target] [dest] Download the room, a folder, or one document, mirroring structure mage mkdir <folder> Create an empty folder, for example 01-Corporate/Charters mage rm <target> [-r|--folder] [-y|--yes] Delete a document, or a folder with --folder mage version Print the CLI version mage help [command] Display help for a command Global flags: --json for machine-readable output on stdout, --api-url <url> to point at a different API base, and -v, --version . Environment variables: MAGE_API_KEY (a room-scoped key that overrides any stored login), MAGE_API_URL (override the API base), MAGE_ROOM_ID (pin the room id rather than resolving it from the key), and MAGE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID (rarely needed; normally discovered from the API). How folder structure survives the trip Point the CLI at a directory and the directory mirrors its contents beneath itself. Point it at a file and the file lands in the folder named by --to , which is created if it does not exist. Dotfiles like .DS_Store and .git are skipped. Uploads run in parallel. mage upload ./diligence mage upload ./charter.pdf --to "01-Corporate" mage mkdir "01-Corporate/Charters" Structure matters more here than in ordinary file storage, because the tree becomes the index. Every folder and filed document receives a stable dotted hierarchical number, the classic VDR convention: 1, 1.2, 1.2.3. Within a level, folders and documents share one number sequence, ordered case-insensitively by display name. Numbers are stored rather than recomputed on every read, so a citation to 4.2.1 stays valid until the room is deliberately re-indexed. One deliberate exception: a document with no folder path sits in Unsorted and is left un-numbered until it is organized into a folder. That is by design, not a gap, and it is the reason to get the tree right before you push. While the files land, the room does its own work. The server classifies each arrival by type, summarizes it, organizes the room in a single pass that chooses the folder structure, and links amendments, exhibits, and side letters to the agreement they belong to. The full walkthrough of a first room setup covers that side. Reading the checklist and filling it The room carries a readiness checklist: the documents an investor's counsel or an acquirer's counsel expects to find, scored per item as present, partial, or missing, with items the user has marked not applicable excluded from the score entirely. mage readiness mage readiness --json mage upload ./tax/2025-return.pdf --for-item <itemId> mage readiness attach <itemId> "Corporate/Bylaws.pdf" --json returns each item with a stable itemId , a label, and a hint describing what the item should contain. --for-item uploads the files and attaches every one that landed to that item, in one step. readiness attach accepts a document id, a name, or folder/name , and is additive: documents already attached stay attached. Per-item curation lives on its own and survives every recompute, so marking something not applicable is not undone by the next pass. That loop is what makes this scriptable. Read what is missing, produce it, attach it, re-read. Handing the same loop to an AI agent is a natural extension, which we cover separately in data rooms in the agentic era . Machine-readable output and headless runs Every command accepts --json and emits machine-readable output on stdout. Combined with a key in the environment, that is the whole headless story: export MAGE_API_KEY="..." mage readiness --json mage upload ./collected --for-item cap-table Setting MAGE_API_KEY skips login entirely. The CLI discovers which room the key belongs to on first use, so the key is all a CI job or an agent needs. On the readiness API specifically, reads and per-item curation accept a room-scoped key, while notify and recompute stay human-gated behind a session. That split is deliberate: a script can fill the room, but it cannot email your investors. Which providers expose a terminal client or an API? Precision matters here, because the marketing in this category is loose. Access path Where it stands as of August 1, 2026 Command-line client on npm None of Datasite, Intralinks, Ideals, Firmex, Ansarada, DealRoom, SecureDocs, Digify, or DocSend publishes one MCP connectors Datasite states an MCP connector for Claude, ChatGPT, or Microsoft Copilot; Ideals promotes an MCP connector on its homepage; DealRoom ships an MCP integration Vendor-published npm executable Papermark publishes @papermark/mcp-server on npm from its own scope and repo API tier gating Ideals gates its MCP connector and API integration to the Enterprise plan Two honest qualifications. Box publishes an official command-line client for the Box API on npm and also sells a virtual data room, so "no data room vendor ships a CLI" is only true of the deal-VDR incumbents, not of the category read broadly. And Mage is not uniquely agent-reachable: Datasite ships an MCP server plus published agent skills targeting sell-side workflows including VDR index setup and information-request-list tracking, and names Claude Code as a supported host. This space is moving fast, and three of those MCP products shipped within the last four months. What remains distinctive is the shape rather than the existence of access. An MCP connector or an enterprise REST integration is something an IT team wires up. A published npm executable is something a founder or an associate runs in ninety seconds, with a credential they can revoke themselves from a settings page. What this CLI will not do Four limits, stated plainly, because a reference that only lists capabilities is a brochure. It drives the data room, and nothing else. mage --help groups every current command under "Data room". Mage's diligence platform has no command-line surface. If you are looking to script disclosure schedules or memos, that is not this tool. There is no unauthenticated path. The shortest honest flow from zero is two commands, not one. Anything shorter is a tutorial for a different product. Deletes are gentler than they look, which cuts both ways. rm --folder moves that folder's documents to Unsorted rather than deleting them, so a scripted cleanup can leave you with a pile of un-numbered documents instead of the clean room you expected. Run ls after. The room has no redaction and no counterparty Q&A module. Ask Mage answers questions from the room's documents for members, and guests do not get it. Neither of those is a CLI limitation; they are product limitations that the CLI cannot route around. For continuous sync from a shared drive, the connector path is the documented one: connect Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, or Box, choose a folder, and Mage keeps the room in sync as new files land. The CLI is for pushes you control, not a background sync daemon. The web path, for everyone else Most of the people you work with will never open a terminal, and they should not have to. Everything above has a browser equivalent: drag in files and folders, drop a ZIP, or connect a cloud drive from the source picker. The room organizes itself the same way, numbers the same way, and shares the same way, through per-recipient invite links carrying view or download permission, an optional expiry, instant revocation, and an NDA gate that is on by default. Pick the interface that matches the person. The terminal for the founder with a folder tree and the platform team with a pipeline; the browser for the deal team. Start either one at Mage Data Room , which is free for a limited time, or read the rest of our writing on rooms in the data rooms resource hub .

title: Galaxy CEO Letter: Growing the Economy that Runs on Code
summary: A letter from Galaxy CEO & Founder, Mike Novogratz, on how digital assets and AI infrastructure are converging, and why Galaxy leads both sides of that shift
body_text: A letter from Galaxy's Founder & CEO, Mike Novogratz — The global financial system runs on infrastructure built for a slower world. That era is ending. The economy is increasingly being rebuilt in code. Two forces are driving it, and they are converging. Finance is moving onchain. Money, markets, and ownership are becoming programmable on rails that settle in seconds and never close. What began on the fringe is now being built by the largest banks and asset managers in the world. More than $300 billion in stablecoins already circulate. Real dollars, moving on code, today. At the same time, artificial intelligence is remaking every industry . And intelligence is hungry for something stubbornly physical: power, land, and the data centers that turn them into compute. Compute is one of the scarcest resources of the decade. The world's largest technology companies are expected to spend hundreds of billions of dollars this year alone just to keep up. It is still not enough. These are not two stories. They are one. The code economy needs programmable rails, and it needs the power to run. Galaxy was built for that convergence. We have spent eight years on a single conviction: that digital assets would remake global finance. Believing it early enough meant we could build the infrastructure instead of renting someone else's. Through bull markets and bear markets, crises and doubt, that conviction held. We acquired Helios at the lows of 2022, when much of the industry was retreating. We won our largest mandates while others pulled back. We put regulated rails, real custody, and tokenization to work while much of the market was still telling stories. Builders do their best work when others have gone to the sidelines. Today that conviction has two proof points: what we own, and who we work with. On infrastructure, Helios is our flagship. Our AI data center campus in West Texas is approved for more than 1.6 gigawatts of capacity , and it is already generating revenue as we build it out to full scale. The anchor lease alone is anticipated to represent over $1 billion in average annual revenue across the fifteen-year term. And Helios is only the first campus in a disciplined, multi-campus build. We are committing to Texas at gigawatt scale, with additional sites in development that could add gigawatts more . From here, the ambition is a portfolio of AI infrastructure spread across geographies, tenants, and technologies. On finance, proof is the roster. BNY, which safeguards tens of trillions of dollars for the world's largest institutions, is bringing staking to its custody platform with Galaxy , and named us a design partner for the next generation of digital-asset infrastructure. With State Street Investment Management, we launched SWEEP , a tokenized fund that brings institutional cash management onchain. Through a referral arrangement with Galaxy, eligible Morgan Stanley Wealth Management clients can lend cryptocurrency to Galaxy and receive shares of spot crypto exchange-traded products. Invesco's bitcoin , Ethereum , and Solana carry the Invesco Galaxy name. And BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, works with Galaxy across its crypto ETFs , from helping to provide liquidity to running a validator node, the same staking we run for Fidelity Investments' crypto ETPs, Morgan Stanley Investment Management and Invesco. These are the biggest names in finance, building alongside Galaxy. Most companies work at one end of this convergence or the other, building the financial rails or the power and compute behind AI. We work at both. That gives us a vantage point few have, and what we build on one side helps the other. The question is no longer whether the economy will be built on code. It is who builds it , and how fast . The answer is Galaxy. -- Mike Novogratz Founder and CEO, Galaxy Legal Disclosure: This document, and the information contained herein, has been provided to you by Galaxy Digital Holdings LP and its affiliates (“Galaxy Digital”) solely for informational purposes. title: How Freelancers in SEA Can Manage Payments with HitPay
summary: How freelancers and service businesses in Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines can collect payments, send invoices, and get paid faster with HitPay.
body_text: Quick Answer: HitPay is a MAS-licensed payment platform that helps freelancers and service businesses in Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines collect payments via payment links, invoices, and local e-wallets — with no monthly fees. Payouts arrive next business day for SGD (Singapore) and PHP (Philippines); T+2 calendar days for MYR (Malaysia). Sign-up is free and approval takes 1–3 business days. Freelance and services work is growing fast across Southeast Asia. According to Google-Temasek e-Conomy SEA , the region’s digital economy continues to expand at pace — and a rising share of that activity involves independent professionals: designers, consultants, tutors, photographers, and personal trainers operating without a fixed business address or retail storefront. For these operators, payment collection is often the weakest link. Clients pay via bank transfer into personal accounts, receipts are informal, and cash flow is unpredictable. A professional payment system is not a luxury — it is a baseline requirement for running a sustainable service business. What Payment Infrastructure Does a Freelance Business Actually Need? Most freelancers do not need a full e-commerce stack. The core requirements are simpler: A way to request payment from a client without a website A method clients can pay using their preferred local app A record of every transaction for bookkeeping Funds settling quickly into a business bank account The right payment setup covers all four without monthly overhead. Understanding the difference between digital wallets and payment gateways helps freelancers choose tools that match how their clients actually prefer to pay — whether that is PayNow in Singapore, DuitNow QR in Malaysia, or GCash in the Philippines. How Do Payment Links Work for Freelancers? Payment links are the most practical tool for service businesses. A payment link is a URL that opens a checkout page — no website required. Freelancers share it via WhatsApp, email, or Instagram, and clients pay immediately. HitPay’s payment links support local payment methods per market, including: Singapore: PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Visa, Mastercard, Atome Malaysia: DuitNow QR, FPX, Touch ‘n Go, GrabPay, Visa, Mastercard Philippines: GCash, Maya, QR Ph, InstaPay, PESONet, Visa, Mastercard A graphic designer in Tanjong Pagar can send a payment link to a client who pays via PayNow in under 30 seconds. A personal trainer in Bangsar can collect session fees through Touch ‘n Go without handling cash. A freelance photographer in Bonifacio Global City (BGC) can bill a corporate client by card and receive funds the next business day. For recurring clients — retainer arrangements or monthly coaching packages — HitPay’s recurring payment links let freelancers set up automated billing cycles without manual follow-up each month. How Should Freelancers Handle Invoicing and Records? Informal billing creates two problems: clients do not pay on time, and reconciliation at tax season becomes chaotic. A structured invoicing workflow solves both. HitPay’s invoicing tool lets freelancers generate branded invoices with itemised line items and attach a payment link directly — so clients receive a professional document and a one-click payment option in the same message. Transactions are logged automatically in the HitPay dashboard, creating a running record of every payment received. This matters for freelancers operating in markets with formal tax obligations: in the Philippines, the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) requires registered self-employed individuals to maintain proper income records. Singapore’s Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) has equivalent requirements for self-employed persons earning above the filing threshold. For a deeper look at how invoice-linked payments work in practice, invoice payment workflows for SMEs in Singapore and Southeast Asia covers the end-to-end process. What Are the Fees and Payout Timelines for Freelancers? HitPay charges no monthly fee and no setup fee. Freelancers pay only per transaction — rates vary by payment method and market (see hitpayapp.com/pricing for current rates). Payout timing by market: Singapore (SGD): next business day Philippines (PHP): next business day Malaysia (MYR): T+2 calendar days Cross-border transactions: T+2 For a freelancer managing cash flow carefully, understanding the distinction between markets matters — particularly when working with clients across borders. HitPay holds a Major Payment Institution licence from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (licence PS20200643) and is PCI DSS compliant — relevant for freelancers handling client card payments who want assurance that data security obligations are met by the platform, not left to them. How Do Freelancers Get Started with HitPay? Go to hitpayapp.com and click Sign Up — no credit card required Submit business details (individual/sole trader registration is accepted) Complete identity verification — approval takes 1–3 business days Add a bank account for payouts Create a payment link or invoice from the dashboard Share the link directly with a client via WhatsApp, email, or any messaging channel Accounts can be approved and accepting payments within 3 business days in most cases. Frequently Asked Questions Can a freelancer (not a registered company) sign up for HitPay? Yes. HitPay accepts sole traders and self-employed individuals, not just registered companies. Freelancers in Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines can sign up using individual business details, though identity verification documents are required during onboarding. How do I collect payment from a client in Singapore without a website? HitPay payment links work without a website. Create a payment link from the HitPay dashboard, set the amount, and send the URL to the client via WhatsApp or email. The client can pay by PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, card, or other supported methods in under a minute. How long does it take to receive funds after a client pays in Malaysia? Domestic transactions in Malaysia (MYR) settle to the linked bank account within T+2 calendar days. Cross-border transactions — for example, a Singapore client paying a Malaysian freelancer — also settle at T+2. What payment methods can Filipino freelancers accept through HitPay? Freelancers in the Philippines can accept GCash, Maya, QR Ph, InstaPay, PESONet, Visa, Mastercard, GrabPay, and ShopeePay through HitPay. Cross-border acceptance includes PayNow (Singapore), QRIS (Indonesia), and PromptPay (Thailand), among others. HitPay vs PayPal — which is better for freelancers in Southeast Asia? HitPay is purpose-built for Southeast Asia and supports local e-wallets (GCash, Touch 'n Go, PayNow, DuitNow) that PayPal does not accept. HitPay also offers next business day domestic payouts in Singapore and the Philippines, no monthly fees, and MAS licensing. PayPal has broader global brand recognition and may suit freelancers billing clients outside Southeast Asia who prefer PayPal's buyer protection. For SEA-based client work, HitPay's local payment method coverage and settlement speed are stronger. Is there a monthly fee to use HitPay as a freelancer? No. HitPay charges no monthly fee and no setup fee. The only cost is a per-transaction fee, which varies by payment method and market. Full pricing is available at hitpayapp.com/pricing. How do I issue a professional invoice and get paid through HitPay? From the HitPay dashboard, navigate to Invoices, create a new invoice with line items and client details, then attach a payment link before sending. The client receives the invoice by email and can pay directly through the embedded link using their preferred payment method.

title: electroCore Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: Second quarter 2026 net sales of $9.5 million, an increase of 28% over $7.4 million in the second quarter 2025 Net loss of $3.1 million decreased 17% from prior year with Adjusted EBITDA net loss improving 26% from prior-year period Increasing 2026 revenue guidance to greater than 30%
body_text: electroCore Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results August 6, 2026 at 4:05 PM EDT Second quarter 2026 net sales of $9.5 million , an increase of 28% over $7.4 million in the second quarter 2025 Net loss of $3.1 million decreased 17% from prior year with Adjusted EBITDA net loss improving 26% from prior-year period Increasing 2026 revenue guidance to greater than 30% year-over-year growth Company to host a conference call and webcast today, August 6, 2026 , at 4:30 pm EDT ROCKAWAY, N.J., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- electroCore, Inc. (Nasdaq: ECOR) (“electroCore” or the “Company”), a bioelectronic technology company, today announced financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. The Company reported quarterly revenue of $9.5 million, an increase of approximately 28% year-over-year, driven by continued growth in U.S. prescription sales in the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (“VA”) and direct-to-consumer Truvaga sales. “This quarter marked a new era for our company as we implemented significant changes across our commercial organization to better position us for long-term success,” said Joshua Lev, Interim President and Chief Financial Officer of electroCore. “While these actions required investment and focus throughout the quarter, we believe they have strengthened our foundation, improved operating efficiency, and enhanced our ability to accelerate revenue growth. We are encouraged by the early results, and we believe these changes will help us drive sustainable top-line growth and achieve positive Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter of 2027.” Recent Operational Highlights Veterans Affairs Channel Continues to Drive Prescription Growth The VA continued to be the Company’s largest growth driver in the second quarter. Prescription (Rx) gammaCore revenue grew approximately 11% year-over-year Approximately 16,400 VA patients have received a gammaCore device, representing approximately 2.7% penetration of the estimated addressable VA headache market. Quell Adoption Accelerates Sales of the Quell product line were $1.3 million in the second quarter of 2026, growing approximately 700% year-over-year and approximately 30% over the first quarter of 2026. Cumulative Quell revenue is approximately $4.0 million since the acquisition from NeuroMetrix, Inc. (“NURO”) in May 2025, of which $3.8 million of Quell Fibromyalgia has been sold into the VA. Truvaga Spend Decreases as Media Costs Expand Truvaga revenue grew approximately 27% year-over-year to $1.3 million and decreased 17% from the prior period. The Company reduced its Truvaga spend in response to higher media pricing. Evolution of the Commercial Organization To promote sustained growth, the Company has made material structural changes to the commercial organization. The Company doubled the number of sales regions from three to six, promoting greater accountability in smaller geographic territories. The Company recruited, contracted, and trained 17 new 1099 representatives with renewed focus on new patients and refill rates at the individual VA account level and helped diversify revenue across a larger number of accounts. These changes are also structured to improve our cost efficiency over time. The Company has redesigned the sales incentive plan to reduce sales and marketing expense as a percentage of revenue. The redesigned plan realigns the Company’s sales territories, eliminating overlapping, inefficient coverage that added cost without building durable accounts and should result in a reduction in incentive compensation variable expense from approximately 35% of prescription revenue to 27% and an overall reduction of the sales and marketing expense to 54% of revenue by the end of 2027. In addition, moving forward Lovell Government Services will be the Company’s primary Federal Supply Schedule contract holder across all electroCore products, in both the VA and DoD markets. That will simplify how the Company’s products move through federal procurement and positions the Company to scale federal growth more efficiently and is expected to eliminate roughly 3% of general and administrative expense in transaction fees associated with direct sales. Beyond the VA, the Company contracted a 1099 representative with a specific mandate to grow the Company’s presence within the Kaiser Permanente Georgia system and hired a W-2 employee to bring dedicated focus and expertise to Department of Defense and federal workers' compensation. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Select Guidance For the three months ended June 30, 2026, electroCore reported net sales of $9.5 million compared to $7.4 million during the same period in 2025, an increase of approximately 28% over the prior year. The increase of $2.1 million was primarily driven by growth in net sales of Quell Fibromyalgia products acquired from NURO in May 2025 and Rx gammaCore, which are sold to the VA, and continued growth in net sales of the Company’s nonprescription general wellness Truvaga products. During the remainder of 2026, the Company intends to generate the majority of its sales in the VA channel through the Company’s agreement with Lovell. Three months ended June 30 , Channel: 2026 2025 United States – Rx $ 7,447 $ 5,693 General Wellness 1,306 1,014 Outside the United States 503 469 TAC-STIM 185 181 In-License / Other 9 24 Total Net Sales $ 9,450 $ 7,381 Six months ended June 30 , Channel: 2026 2025 United States – Rx $ 14,868 $ 10,703 General Wellness 2,894 2,114 Outside the United States 1,005 967 TAC-STIM 227 271 In-License / Other 40 45 Total Net Sales $ 19,034 $ 14,100 Gross profit increased $1.7 million to $8.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase in gross profit is attributable to the increased net sales. Gross margin decreased from 87.3% to 86.5% for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025. The decrease in gross margin was primarily due to an increase in our inventory reserve. Research and development expense was $0.8 million in the second quarter of 2026, compared to $0.5 million in the second quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to increased studies and grants, higher stock-based compensation, and initial costs to develop enhancements to our Truvaga mobile application. Selling, general and administrative expense was $10.1 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $9.4 million in the prior year period. Sales and marketing increased $1.4 million from the prior year. The increase in sales and marketing expense was primarily driven by approximately $0.9 million of variable expenses that supported the $2.1 million increase in net sales, reflecting the operating leverage embedded in the Company’s platform as it scales. General and administrative expense decreased $0.7 million from the prior year. The decrease was primarily attributable to $0.5 million in bad debt expense recorded in the second quarter of 2025 (associated with a TAC-STIM receivable) that did not recur, as well as a reduction in professional fees in the second quarter of 2026. Total operating expenses in the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $10.9 million, compared to $9.9 million in the three months ended June 30, 2025. GAAP net loss in the second quarter of 2026 was $3.1 million, compared to $3.7 million in the second quarter of 2025. The decrease in GAAP net loss was primarily attributed to higher gross profit associated with the increase in net sales, partially offset by variable sales and marketing expenses associated with the increase in sales. Net loss per share for the second quarter of 2026 was $0.33, compared to $0.44 in the second quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA net loss in the second quarter of 2026 was $1.8 million, compared to an adjusted EBITDA net loss of $2.4 million in the second quarter of 2025, an improvement of approximately $0.6 million, or 26%, year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA net loss is a non-GAAP financial measure. See “Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measure” below for additional information and a reconciliation to GAAP net loss. Total cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities at June 30, 2026, was approximately $10.0 million, compared to approximately $11.6 million at December 31, 2025. Full Year 2026 and Select 2027 Outlook The Company is raising its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to greater than 30% annual growth over full-year 2025 and expects to achieve positive Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter of 2027. title: Modal, Operasional, dan Strategi Bisnis Laundry
summary: Panduan lengkap bisnis laundry: jenis usaha, modal awal, break-even, pricing, hingga solusi pembayaran digital untuk pemula.
body_text: Bisnis laundry adalah usaha jasa cuci dan setrika pakaian yang menyasar konsumen dengan mobilitas tinggi dan keterbatasan waktu untuk mencuci sendiri. Potensinya tetap besar karena kebutuhan mencuci pakaian bersifat rutin dan tidak tergantung musim, sehingga arus kas cenderung stabil sepanjang tahun. Artikel ini membahas seluruh aspek yang perlu dipahami sebelum dan sesudah membuka usaha laundry, mulai dari jenis model bisnis, perhitungan modal dan break-even, strategi lokasi, penetapan harga, hingga solusi pembayaran digital yang sering luput dibahas di panduan laundry pada umumnya. Mengapa Bisnis Laundry Masih Potensial di 2026 Permintaan jasa laundry didorong oleh perubahan gaya hidup urban: makin banyak pekerja kantoran, mahasiswa, dan keluarga muda yang memilih outsourcing pekerjaan rumah tangga demi efisiensi waktu. Karakteristik permintaan yang berulang (repeat order) membuat model bisnis ini relatif tahan terhadap fluktuasi ekonomi dibanding usaha musiman. Selain itu, hambatan masuk (barrier to entry) tergolong moderat. Modal bisa disesuaikan mulai dari skala rumahan dengan satu-dua mesin, hingga skala outlet profesional dengan kapasitas besar. Ini menjadikan laundry pilihan populer bagi career switcher maupun calon wirausahawan pemula. Jenis-Jenis Bisnis Laundry Sebelum menentukan skala investasi, penting memahami beberapa model laundry yang umum beroperasi di Indonesia. Laundry Kiloan Model paling umum di area perumahan dan kampus. Pakaian ditimbang per kilogram, dicuci dan dikeringkan secara massal tanpa pemilahan mendetail. Cocok untuk target pasar mahasiswa dan pekerja dengan anggaran terbatas. Laundry Satuan / Dry Cleaning Melayani pakaian bernilai tinggi seperti jas, gaun, atau bahan yang memerlukan penanganan khusus. Harga per item lebih mahal, margin lebih tinggi, namun membutuhkan mesin dan bahan kimia dry cleaning yang lebih spesifik. Laundry Sepatu dan Tas Segmen niche yang berkembang pesat, terutama di kota besar. Modal peralatan lebih kecil dibanding laundry kiloan, tetapi menuntut keterampilan khusus dalam deep cleaning material kulit, kanvas, dan suede. Laundry Koin (Self-Service) Pelanggan mengoperasikan mesin sendiri menggunakan koin atau kartu prabayar. Model ini menghemat biaya tenaga kerja karena tidak memerlukan operator penuh waktu, tetapi membutuhkan investasi mesin berkualitas komersial di awal. Perbedaan Model Bisnis Laundry: Mana yang Cocok untuk Anda Model Modal Awal Margin per Transaksi Kebutuhan Tenaga Kerja Laundry Kiloan Rendah-Sedang Sedang Tinggi (operator cuci, setrika, packing) Dry Cleaning Tinggi Tinggi Sedang (butuh keahlian khusus) Laundry Sepatu/Tas Rendah Tinggi Rendah-Sedang Laundry Koin Tinggi (mesin komersial) Rendah per unit, volume tinggi Rendah Bagi pemula dengan modal terbatas, laundry kiloan atau laundry sepatu sering menjadi titik masuk yang lebih realistis sebelum ekspansi ke dry cleaning atau laundry koin yang membutuhkan investasi mesin lebih besar. Modal Awal Bisnis Laundry Estimasi modal awal sangat bergantung pada skala dan model yang dipilih. Berikut breakdown komponen biaya utama untuk laundry kiloan skala rumahan hingga menengah. Breakdown Biaya Peralatan Mesin cuci kapasitas 8-10 kg: Rp4.000.000 – Rp8.000.000 per unit Mesin pengering (dryer): Rp5.000.000 – Rp10.000.000 per unit Setrika uap dan meja setrika: Rp1.000.000 – Rp2.500.000 Timbangan digital: Rp300.000 – Rp600.000 Rak, keranjang, dan plastik packing: Rp1.500.000 – Rp3.000.000 Deterjen dan bahan kimia awal: Rp1.000.000 – Rp2.000.000 Signage dan interior sederhana: Rp2.000.000 – Rp5.000.000 Dengan dua unit mesin cuci dan satu pengering, total modal peralatan berkisar Rp15.000.000 hingga Rp30.000.000, belum termasuk sewa tempat dan modal kerja bulan pertama. Biaya Operasional Bulanan Sewa tempat: Rp1.500.000 – Rp5.000.000 (tergantung lokasi) Listrik dan air: Rp1.000.000 – Rp2.500.000 Gaji karyawan (1-2 orang): Rp2.500.000 – Rp5.000.000 Deterjen dan bahan pendukung: Rp800.000 – Rp1.500.000 Biaya pemasaran: Rp300.000 – Rp1.000.000 Break-Even Point dan Proyeksi Profit Break-even point (BEP) adalah titik di mana total pendapatan menyamai total biaya, sehingga usaha belum untung namun juga tidak rugi. Memahami BEP penting agar target omzet harian dan bulanan lebih terukur, bukan sekadar estimasi kasar. Contoh Simulasi Break-Even Asumsikan harga jasa laundry kiloan Rp7.000/kg dengan biaya variabel (deterjen, listrik, air per kg) sekitar Rp2.500/kg. Margin kontribusi per kg adalah Rp4.500. Jika biaya tetap bulanan (sewa, gaji, listrik dasar) sebesar Rp6.000.000, maka volume BEP dihitung sebagai berikut. BEP (kg) = Biaya Tetap Bulanan ÷ Margin Kontribusi per Kg = Rp6.000.000 ÷ Rp4.500 ≈ 1.334 kg per bulan, atau sekitar 45 kg per hari. Dengan modal awal Rp20.000.000 dan rata-rata profit bersih Rp2.000.000-Rp4.000.000 per bulan setelah melewati BEP, payback period yang realistis berada di kisaran 6-10 bulan, tergantung konsistensi volume order dan efisiensi operasional. Menentukan Lokasi Strategis Lokasi menjadi faktor penentu volume order harian. Beberapa segmen lokasi yang terbukti efektif: Sekitar kampus dan kos-kosan: volume tinggi dari mahasiswa, cocok untuk laundry kiloan dengan harga kompetitif. Area perumahan padat penduduk: pelanggan keluarga dengan kebutuhan rutin, potensi langganan bulanan lebih stabil. Dekat perkantoran atau apartemen: target pekerja dengan daya beli lebih tinggi, cocok untuk layanan antar-jemput dan dry cleaning. Pusat perbelanjaan atau area komersial: cocok untuk laundry sepatu dan layanan ekspres dengan margin lebih tinggi. Segmentasi customer sebaiknya disesuaikan dengan karakteristik lokasi. Laundry di area kampus umumnya bersaing di harga, sementara laundry di area perumahan menengah ke atas dapat bersaing di kualitas dan kenyamanan layanan antar-jemput. Strategi Pricing Jasa Laundry Penetapan harga tidak boleh sekadar mengikuti kompetitor terdekat. Berikut pendekatan pricing yang lebih terukur. Pricing Berbasis Biaya (Cost-Plus) Hitung Harga Pokok Produksi (HPP) per kg mencakup deterjen, listrik, air, dan proporsi biaya tenaga kerja, lalu tambahkan margin yang diinginkan. Pendekatan ini memastikan setiap transaksi tetap menghasilkan profit, bukan hanya menutup biaya. Sistem Pricing Dinamis Beberapa usaha laundry menerapkan pricing bertingkat berdasarkan kecepatan layanan, misalnya reguler (2-3 hari), express (1 hari), dan same-day service dengan harga premium. Model ini memungkinkan segmentasi pelanggan berdasarkan urgensi kebutuhan, sekaligus meningkatkan rata-rata pendapatan per pelanggan tanpa menaikkan harga dasar. Paket Berlangganan Paket bulanan dengan kuota kilogram tertentu dapat meningkatkan retensi pelanggan dan memberikan kepastian arus kas bulanan, dibanding hanya mengandalkan transaksi satuan yang fluktuatif. Manajemen Inventory dan Bahan Baku Pengelolaan persediaan yang buruk sering menjadi penyebab tersembunyi kebocoran biaya di bisnis laundry. Beberapa praktik yang perlu diterapkan: Catat pemakaian deterjen dan pewangi per siklus cuci untuk mengontrol biaya variabel secara akurat. Tetapkan stok minimum bahan kimia agar operasional tidak terhenti saat permintaan naik. Gunakan sistem pencatatan sederhana (spreadsheet atau aplikasi kasir) untuk melacak penggunaan plastik packing, hanger, dan label. Lakukan stock opname berkala untuk mendeteksi selisih antara catatan dan stok fisik. Sistem kasir digital yang terintegrasi dengan pencatatan inventory dapat membantu mengotomatiskan pelacakan ini, sehingga pemilik tidak perlu menghitung manual setiap akhir bulan. Marketing Media Sosial untuk Bisnis Laundry Promosi digital menjadi kanal akuisisi pelanggan yang murah dan terukur dibanding iklan konvensional. Beberapa taktik yang efektif untuk usaha laundry lokal: Manfaatkan Instagram dan TikTok untuk konten before-after hasil cuci, terutama untuk segmen laundry sepatu dan dry cleaning. Daftarkan bisnis di Google Maps dengan foto, jam operasional, dan ulasan pelanggan untuk meningkatkan visibilitas pencarian lokal. Gunakan WhatsApp Business untuk layanan pemesanan antar-jemput dan konfirmasi otomatis. Berikan insentif referral bagi pelanggan yang mengajak teman atau tetangga berlangganan. Operasional Harian Laundry Alur kerja harian yang konsisten membantu menjaga kualitas layanan sekaligus efisiensi waktu. Urutan umum meliputi penerimaan dan penimbangan pakaian, pencatatan pesanan, proses cuci-kering, penyortiran dan setrika, packing, hingga konfirmasi pengambilan atau pengantaran. Standarisasi proses ini penting terutama saat bisnis mulai memiliki lebih dari satu karyawan, agar kualitas hasil tidak bergantung pada satu orang saja. Solusi Pembayaran Digital untuk Bisnis Laundry Sistem pembayaran menjadi bagian operasional yang sering diabaikan pada tahap awal, padahal berdampak langsung pada kecepatan transaksi dan pencatatan keuangan. Menerima pembayaran tunai saja membuat rekonsiliasi kas rawan selisih dan menyulitkan pelacakan omzet harian. Mengadopsi QRIS memungkinkan pelanggan membayar langsung dari aplikasi perbankan atau e-wallet mana pun tanpa perlu uang pas, sekaligus memberikan pemilik usaha catatan transaksi otomatis yang memudahkan pembukuan. Untuk usaha laundry dengan volume transaksi tinggi seperti model kiloan, kombinasi QRIS dan EDC juga membantu mempercepat antrean saat jam sibuk, terutama saat pelanggan mengambil pakaian bersamaan di sore hari. Integrasi sistem pembayaran digital dengan pencatatan kasir juga mempermudah pemilik memantau omzet real-time tanpa harus menghitung manual setiap hari, sekaligus mengurangi risiko kehilangan uang tunai di lokasi usaha. Staff Management Untuk laundry skala kiloan dengan volume harian tinggi, kebutuhan tenaga kerja minimal mencakup operator cuci-kering, staf setrika dan packing, serta kasir. Pada skala rumahan, satu orang bisa merangkap beberapa peran, namun seiring pertumbuhan volume, pemisahan tugas membantu menjaga konsistensi kualitas dan kecepatan layanan. Berikan pelatihan dasar mengenai standar pemisahan pakaian (warna, bahan, tingkat kotor) serta SOP penanganan komplain, karena kesalahan pencucian sering menjadi sumber utama ketidakpuasan pelanggan. Analisis Kompetitor Sebelum menentukan harga dan lokasi, lakukan survei terhadap 3-5 usaha laundry terdekat mencakup rentang harga per kg, waktu proses, layanan tambahan (antar-jemput, express), dan ulasan pelanggan di Google Maps. Data ini membantu menentukan posisi harga yang kompetitif sekaligus mengidentifikasi celah layanan yang belum digarap kompetitor, misalnya opsi pembayaran digital atau layanan same-day yang belum tersedia di area tersebut. Scaling ke Multi-Outlet Setelah operasional outlet pertama stabil dan menghasilkan profit konsisten selama beberapa bulan, ekspansi ke outlet kedua dapat dipertimbangkan. Beberapa hal yang perlu dipersiapkan sebelum scaling: SOP tertulis yang terdokumentasi untuk seluruh proses operasional, sehingga outlet baru tidak bergantung pada supervisi langsung pemilik. Sistem pencatatan keuangan terpusat agar omzet dan biaya setiap outlet dapat dipantau secara terpisah maupun agregat. Standarisasi sistem pembayaran digital di seluruh outlet agar rekonsiliasi kas lebih mudah dan konsisten. Perhitungan ulang break-even point untuk outlet baru, karena biaya sewa dan karakteristik lokasi bisa berbeda signifikan. FAQ Modal minimal untuk laundry rumahan skala kecil dengan satu mesin cuci dan satu pengering berkisar Rp8.000.000 hingga Rp15.000.000, tergantung kondisi mesin (baru atau bekas) dan kelengkapan awal seperti deterjen dan kemasan. Payback period rata-rata usaha laundry kiloan berkisar 6-12 bulan, tergantung volume order harian, efisiensi biaya operasional, dan konsistensi pemasaran di bulan-bulan awal. Usaha laundry skala kecil-menengah umumnya cukup mendaftarkan Nomor Induk Berusaha (NIB) melalui sistem OSS (Online Single Submission) sebagai legalitas dasar, tanpa memerlukan izin operasional khusus seperti industri pengolahan berskala besar. Laundry kiloan mengandalkan volume tinggi dengan margin per transaksi lebih rendah, sedangkan dry cleaning menyasar pakaian bernilai tinggi dengan margin lebih besar per item namun volume transaksi yang lebih rendah dan kebutuhan keahlian khusus. Hitung HPP per kg (deterjen, listrik, air, proporsi tenaga kerja), tambahkan margin yang diinginkan, lalu bandingkan dengan rentang harga kompetitor di area yang sama untuk memastikan harga tetap kompetitif tanpa mengorbankan profitabilitas. Ya, pembayaran digital seperti QRIS membantu mempercepat transaksi saat jam sibuk, mengurangi risiko uang tunai hilang atau selisih kas, dan memudahkan pemilik memantau omzet secara real-time untuk pengambilan keputusan bisnis. Menjalankan bisnis laundry lebih efisien saat sistem pembayaran dan pencatatan transaksi sudah terdigitalisasi sejak awal. Dengan Payfazz, Anda dapat mendaftarkan QRIS untuk menerima pembayaran dari berbagai bank dan e-wallet, memanfaatkan solusi EDC untuk transaksi kartu, serta mencatat setiap transaksi secara otomatis tanpa perlu pembukuan manual.
