title: What Is App Store Connect? A Beginner’s Guide
summary: App Store Connect is Apple’s hub for publishing and managing apps. App Review, TestFlight, purchases, analytics, reviews, and updates explained for beginners.
body_text: You finished building your app in Xcode, Bitrig, or another tool. You’ve tested it, fixed the obvious bugs, and polished the interface. Now, how do you actually get it onto the App Store? That’s where App Store Connect comes in. App Store Connect helps you take an app from a finished build to a real product that people can discover, download, review, and purchase. You’ll use it for your first launch, but you’ll keep coming back whenever you release an update, add a subscription, check your sales, run a beta test, or respond to a customer. What is App Store Connect? App Store Connect is Apple’s web-based service for managing apps distributed through the App Store. It doesn’t replace Xcode or Bitrig. Those are tools you use to build, run, and test your app. App Store Connect manages the distribution and business side of the app. To publish an app, you’ll need a paid Apple Developer Program membership. As of 2026, the standard membership costs $99 per year in the U.S. There’s no separate App Store Connect subscription fee on top of that membership. You can learn more about what the membership includes in our guide to the Apple Developer Program. What can you do in App Store Connect? App Store Connect covers almost every part of running an app business once you’re preparing to distribute your app. You can use it to: Create and update your App Store product page Upload and manage app builds Submit apps and updates to App Review Choose where and when your app is released Run beta tests with TestFlight Create subscriptions and in-app purchases Set prices and availability View downloads, sales, proceeds, and engagement Read and respond to customer reviews Manage team members and permissions Complete agreements, tax forms, and banking information Let’s look at the parts new developers are most likely to use. Create your App Store product page Your product page is the public listing people see when they discover your app on the App Store. Most of the information on that page is entered through App Store Connect, including: App name Subtitle Description Keywords Category Screenshots and app previews Support and marketing URLs Privacy information Age rating Promotional text Version release notes Every part of this page can affect whether someone downloads your app. Your screenshots, icon, title, subtitle, description, ratings, and pricing all help users decide whether the app looks relevant and trustworthy. You can learn how to improve these elements in our beginner’s guide to App Store Optimization. Localize your product page for different languages App Store Connect also lets you localize your product page for different languages and regions. For example, you can provide separate Spanish versions of your description, keywords, screenshots, and other metadata. Customers using the App Store in Spanish can then see and search using the localized information. This is separate from translating the interface inside your app. Your app’s interface is localized in your Xcode project, while the information displayed on the App Store is localized through App Store Connect. Bitrig’s App Store Connect integration can generate translations and update your product page through AI, saving you a ton of time as you expand into additional markets. Upload your app and submit it to App Review App Store Connect is where you manage your App Store submission. The process looks like this: Create an app record in App Store Connect. Archive and upload a compiled build from Xcode, Bitrig, or another supported tool. Wait for Apple to process the build. Complete your product page and required app information. Answer the app privacy and age-rating questions. Select the build you want to release. Add the version to a submission. Submit it to App Review. If Apple approves your submission, you can release it manually, release it automatically after approval, or schedule it for a later date. Approval also doesn’t mean the app must immediately appear everywhere. You control the countries and regions where it will be available. You’ll repeat a similar process whenever you submit an update. Create a new version, upload a new build, add your release notes, and send it through App Review again. Apple’s App Review Guidelines explain the technical, design, content, and business rules apps must follow. Manage subscriptions and in-app purchases If your app makes money through digital purchases, much of that setup happens in App Store Connect. You can create: Consumable in-app purchases , such as game currency or AI credits that users can buy more than once Non-consumable purchases , such as a permanent feature unlock Auto-renewable subscriptions , such as weekly, monthly, or annual premium plans Non-renewing subscriptions , which provide access for a fixed period but don’t renew automatically For subscriptions, you can configure pricing, subscription groups, introductory offers, and free trials. Apple supports several trial lengths, depending on the offer you choose. Make sure you check out the App Store Small Business Program . If you qualify, it reduces Apple's commission from 30% to 15%, which is significant savings for your app business. There are two sides to adding purchases. You configure the products, pricing, and availability in App Store Connect, then use StoreKit in your app to display those products, process transactions, and unlock the purchased content. RevenueCat is another good option. If this sounds like a lot… to be honest, it is. Bitrig can automate much of this setup across your Swift code and App Store Connect, including creating in-app purchase products and subscription groups. We can take all of this off your plate. Beta test your app with TestFlight TestFlight is Apple’s beta-testing system, and you manage it through App Store Connect. You can upload a build, specify what you want people to test, organize testers into groups, collect feedback, and review screenshots or crash reports submitted by testers. As of 2026, Apple allows: Up to 100 internal testers who are App Store Connect users Up to 10,000 external testers A testing period of up to 90 days for each build External testing may require a shorter beta review from Apple before the build can be distributed. This is separate from the full App Review process required for a public release. TestFlight is a great way to find crashes, confusing interfaces, and unexpected behavior before those problems reach your App Store customers. You can learn more in Apple’s TestFlight overview . Understand your app’s App Store analytics Once your app is live, App Store Connect shows how people are discovering and using it. You can track metrics such as: Impressions Product page views Conversion rate First-time downloads Redownloads Sales and proceeds Paying users Subscription starts and renewals Sessions Active devices Crashes App deletions Apple’s Analytics interface provides more than 100 metrics across its different reports and features. You can filter many of them by territory, device type, source, app version, and other dimensions. These numbers can help you understand where your App Store funnel is breaking down. For example, imagine your app receives plenty of impressions but very few product page views. People are seeing the app in search results or another App Store placement, but they aren’t tapping to learn more. That could mean you need to improve your: App icon Name or subtitle First screenshots Ratings Keyword relevance Positioning against competing apps If people visit your product page but don’t download the app, look more closely at the complete screenshot set, description, pricing, reviews, and whether the app clearly solves the problem they searched for. Analytics isn’t perfect. Some reports only appear after your app reaches minimum data thresholds, and certain usage metrics are based on users who agreed to share analytics with developers. Treat the numbers as useful signals, not a complete record of every user action. Read and respond to App Store reviews App Store Connect lets you see your app’s ratings and written customer reviews. You can also post a public response to a review and I highly recommend doing this, especially when someone reports a bug, crash, or confusing experience. You don’t need to be defensive or write a long explanation. A simple response can work: Thanks for reporting this. We found the issue and have a fix coming in the next update. We appreciate you letting us know. A good response shows that there’s a real person behind the app and that user feedback matters. Customers can update their rating or review later, although there’s no guarantee that responding will change their rating. Even when the reviewer never returns, your response is visible to other people considering the app. Apple has a complete guide to responding to App Store reviews . Manage sales, payments, and your development team App Store Connect also handles some of the less exciting but very important parts of running an app business. You can use it to: Accept legal agreements Enter tax information Add banking details View sales and proceeds Download financial reports Check completed payments You can also invite other people and assign roles based on what they need to do. Available roles include Admin, Finance, App Manager, Developer, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Support. For example, someone with the Customer Support role can respond to reviews without receiving permission to change your app’s pricing or submit a new build. The Account Holder has complete access and is the only person who can perform certain legal and account-level actions. Can I automate App Store Connect? Yes. Apple provides an App Store Connect API for automating supported app-management tasks. Developers and services can use API keys with specific roles and permissions. Tools such as Bitrig can use App Store Connect workflows to create app records, upload builds, manage listings, capture screenshots, and submit apps for review. Is there an App Store Connect mobile app? Yes. Apple offers an App Store Connect app for iPhone and iPad. The mobile app doesn’t replace every part of the website, but you can use it to monitor app status, manage submissions, work with TestFlight builds and testers, view performance and sales, receive notifications, and respond to customer reviews. It’s especially useful when you’re waiting for an app to move through review or want to keep an eye on a new release. You can download the App Store Connect app from the App Store. Frequently asked questions Is App Store Connect the same as Xcode? No. Xcode is Apple’s development environment for writing, building, running, and testing apps. App Store Connect manages your app’s distribution and App Store presence. You upload a compiled build from Xcode or another development tool, then select and submit that build through App Store Connect. Do I need to pay for App Store Connect? App Store Connect doesn’t have a separate subscription fee, but you generally need a paid Apple Developer Program membership to publish apps, distribute TestFlight builds, and use its App Store distribution features. As of 2026, the standard Apple Developer Program membership is $99 per year in the United States. Can I use App Store Connect before my app is live? Yes. You’ll use App Store Connect before launch to create the app record, prepare the product page, upload builds, run TestFlight betas, configure purchases, and submit the app for review. Is TestFlight the same as App Store Connect? No. TestFlight is Apple’s system for installing and testing beta apps. App Store Connect is the larger management platform where you upload builds, create tester groups, invite TestFlight users, review feedback, and manage the rest of your App Store presence. Can someone else manage my app in App Store Connect? Yes. The Account Holder or an Admin can invite other users and assign roles. Permissions can be limited based on the person’s responsibilities. You could give a developer access to builds, a marketer access to product-page information, or a support person access to customer reviews. The bottom line App Store Connect is the command center for your app once you’re ready to distribute it. It’s where you create your App Store listing, upload and select builds, submit your app for review, manage TestFlight, configure purchases, track performance, respond to reviews, and release future updates. You don’t need to understand every section on your first day. Start with the basic publishing flow: Join the Apple Developer Program. Create your app record. Upload a tested build. Complete your product-page information. Run a TestFlight beta. Submit the app to App Review. Once your app is live, return to App Store Connect regularly to learn from your analytics, monitor reviews, and improve each new version. Try Bitrig When you’re ready to build and publish your first app, Bitrig helps new developers create native Swift apps with AI. Bitrig can also handle most of the App Store Connect workflow, including creating your app record, uploading builds, managing your listing, and submitting the app for review. Try it today.

title: Conta PJ para MEI, microempresa e LTDA e o que muda na gestão em cada fase do negócio
summary: Descubra o que muda, na prática, na gestão de um negócio com uma conta PJ para uma empresa que é MEI, microempresa ou LTDA.
body_text: Quando o dono deixa de fazer tudo sozinho, a conta empresarial muda de função. Para o MEI , o foco é separar o dinheiro do negócio , receber e pagar com clareza. Na microempresa , entram conciliação de vendas, reserva, despesas da equipe e visão de caixa. Numa LTDA com sócios ou gestores, passam a pesar permissões, aprovações, integração e histórico das movimentações. Conta PJ é a conta usada para concentrar os recebimentos, pagamentos e controles financeiros vinculados ao CNPJ. Na Stone, o banco para quem empreende, reunimos conta, maquininha, Pix, cartão, crédito e ferramentas de gestão no mesmo app. Uma conta PJ bem escolhida acompanha três mudanças: o volume de entradas, o número de pessoas que movimentam dinheiro e a complexidade da operação. A sigla da empresa importa, mas a rotina do caixa diz muito mais sobre os recursos que você vai usar. Antes de escolher, entenda o que mudou na empresa MEI, microempresa e sociedade limitada não são três degraus da mesma classificação. A Lei Complementar nº 123 trata a microempresa pelo porte e reúne as regras próprias do MEI. Já o Código Civil define a sociedade limitada pela forma jurídica e pelas responsabilidades previstas no contrato social. Na lei, microempresa descreve o porte, enquanto LTDA descreve a natureza jurídica. Uma sociedade limitada pode, inclusive, ser enquadrada como microempresa quando atende aos critérios legais. Do mesmo jeito, nem toda microempresa precisa ter sócios. Essa diferença muda os documentos exigidos no cadastro, mas não resolve sozinha qual conta combina com a operação. Uma loja LTDA com dois sócios pode ter uma rotina financeira mais simples que a de um MEI que vende no balcão, pelas redes sociais e por entregas. Pra entender sua fase, olhe o caminho do dinheiro: Quantas vendas entram por dia? Quantas pessoas fazem compras em nome da empresa? Há folha, aluguel, imposto, fornecedores e parcelas vencendo em datas diferentes? O contador precisa receber extratos e comprovantes todo mês? Quanto mais respostas entram nessa conta, mais você precisa de controle. O estágio financeiro do negócio aparece no número de decisões que dependem do saldo , não apenas no nome registrado no CNPJ . A mudança de fase também não precisa esperar uma alteração formal. Se você continua como MEI, mas já recebe por diferentes canais, compra estoque toda semana e depende de previsibilidade, a gestão precisa acompanhar essa realidade agora. No MEI, a conta precisa tirar o dinheiro do improviso O Portal do Empreendedor informa que abrir uma conta bancária PJ não é uma obrigação do MEI . Mesmo assim, concentrar a movimentação do negócio em uma conta separada deixa as vendas, os pagamentos e as retiradas mais fáceis de acompanhar. O primeiro ganho é saber quanto a empresa realmente tem. Se o Pix dos clientes cai na mesma conta usada pra pagar supermercado, aluguel de casa e assinatura de streaming, o extrato vira uma mistura. O saldo pode parecer alto de manhã e desaparecer antes da compra de estoque. No MEI, a conta PJ precisa criar uma fronteira clara entre o que pertence ao negócio e o que pertence ao dono. Se essas três informações exigem uma tarde de planilha, a operação está gastando tempo demais pra entender o próprio caixa. A conciliação ganha peso aqui. Assim, uma obrigação previsível não precisa disputar saldo com as compras do dia. O crédito também passa a ter outra função. Crédito entra como alavanca para um movimento calculado, como comprar equipamento, reforçar estoque ou abrir uma nova unidade. Uma dica é, antes de contratar, colocar na ponta do lápis o custo da operação, o prazo e o retorno esperado. Se comprar mais estoque permite negociar um preço melhor e vender dentro de um prazo conhecido, existe uma conta concreta a fazer. Se o dinheiro vai cobrir uma despesa recorrente sem corrigir a origem do aperto, primeiro revise margem, prazos e retiradas. Na LTDA, regras de acesso pesam tanto quanto tarifas A sigla LTDA não indica automaticamente uma empresa maior. Ela mostra que o negócio segue a estrutura jurídica de sociedade limitada, inclusive quando existe apenas um sócio. A conta, por isso, precisa refletir quem administra a empresa e quem pode movimentar os recursos. Nesse estágio, confira se a conta permite organizar acessos, aprovações e limites de movimentação de acordo com a responsabilidade de cada pessoa. Quem lança um pagamento não precisa, necessariamente, ser a mesma pessoa que aprova. Quem compra material pra uma unidade também não precisa enxergar todas as informações da empresa. O contrato social e o cadastro bancário precisam caminhar juntos. Quando há mudança de sócio, administrador, endereço ou atividade, os dados da conta devem ser atualizados. Não adianta o sistema mostrar uma venda que o extrato não identifica, nem o extrato trazer um valor que ninguém consegue associar à loja de origem. Quanto mais unidades e canais existem, mais caro fica conferir tudo manualmente. Atendimento entra nessa escolha pelo mesmo motivo. Quando um pagamento de fornecedor, uma folha ou uma compra estratégica depende da conta, ficar preso em respostas automáticas pode parar a operação. Por isso, procure um canal que consiga entender o contexto e agir no tempo de quem está com o negócio rodando. Se o negócio cresceu, mas tudo continua passando por uma única pessoa, o problema pode estar no processo e nas ferramentas disponíveis. Use estes sinais pra fazer a revisão: Todos os canais de venda aparecem de forma identificável no controle financeiro? Impostos, folha, estoque e outras despesas previstas têm dinheiro separado antes do vencimento? Funcionários ou sócios conseguem cumprir suas funções sem compartilhar a senha pessoal do dono? Extratos e comprovantes chegam à contabilidade sem uma caça mensal a arquivos? O saldo disponível pode ser diferenciado do dinheiro já comprometido? Cartão, recebimentos, reserva e crédito conversam com a mesma visão de caixa? Se várias respostas forem negativas, manter a conta como está custa horas de conferência, retrabalho e decisões feitas com informação incompleta. A tarifa mensal pode até ser baixa, mas ela não mostra sozinha quanto a operação perde quando o dinheiro fica espalhado. Para o MEI, simplicidade e separação costumam vir primeiro. Na microempresa, integração, conciliação e reserva passam a decidir a qualidade do controle. Numa LTDA com mais pessoas na gestão, regras de acesso e histórico das movimentações entram no centro da escolha. Na Conta PJ Stone , você reúne os recursos financeiros do negócio em um só app e pode adicionar produtos conforme a operação avança. A conta acompanha o dia de hoje sem deixar o crescimento de amanhã depender de mais uma planilha improvisada. Este conteúdo é uma forma de apoiar empreendedores na sua jornada. title: How to Write Meeting Notes: Templates & Best Practices (August 2026)
summary: August 2026 guide to structuring meeting notes. Covers templates, action item format, distribution tips, and how AI tools capture decisions automatically.
body_text: Learning how to structure meeting notes well is one of those things nobody really teaches you, and then suddenly you’re the one everyone looks to for the recap. The good news is there’s a clear format that works across almost every meeting type, and once it clicks, you’ll never sit down to a blank doc again. TLDR: Meeting notes are informal and flexible; meeting minutes are formal records with legal standing. Every action item needs a named owner, a specific deliverable, and a clear deadline to drive follow-through. Send notes within 24 hours and store them in one location. Project management tools keep action items tied directly to work. AI-generated notes still need a human review pass to catch misattributed speakers and garbled decisions. Spinach AI is an enterprise conversation intelligence system that organizations deploy company-wide across Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Slack Huddles, and Webex, capturing decisions and action items with named owners and routing structured output to your team’s tools when the meeting ends. Meeting Notes vs. Meeting Minutes Meeting notes and meeting minutes are often used interchangeably, but they serve different purposes and carry different expectations. Meeting notes are informal, flexible records. You capture what seems useful: key points, ideas, follow-ups, anything that helps you or your team act on what was discussed. There is no required format. Meeting minutes are formal, structured documents, typically used for board meetings, legal proceedings, or governance contexts. They record decisions, votes, and attendance as an official record, often with legal standing. What to Include in Well-Structured Meeting Notes Six elements show up in every set of meeting notes worth keeping, regardless of meeting type or length. Date, time, and attendee list Agenda topics covered Key discussion points per topic Decisions reached and who made them Action items with a named owner and a due date Open questions or items parked for a future meeting The most commonly skipped item is the last one. Unresolved questions left undocumented tend to resurface in the next meeting without context, repeating the same discussion from scratch. One other note on meeting notes action items : “someone will follow up on the budget” is not an action item. “Maya will send the revised Q3 budget to the team by Thursday” is. Named owner, specific deliverable, clear deadline. That distinction is what separates notes that drive follow-through from notes that get filed and forgotten. How to Prepare Before the Meeting Good preparation takes about five minutes and removes most of the cognitive strain from live note-taking. Trying to decide what matters while simultaneously following the conversation is where things fall through. Before the meeting starts, three steps help: Read the agenda and note the intended outcome for each topic, beyond the topic label Set up a notes template structured around those agenda items so you have a skeleton ready to fill in Clarify your role: capturing everything versus tracking only decisions and action items requires different focus That third step matters more than it sounds. A note-taker trying to record every word will miss the decision that just got made. One focused on outcomes and named owners can let surrounding discussion flow past without losing anything worth keeping. If there’s no agenda, ask for one or sketch the expected discussion arc based on the meeting’s stated purpose. Walking in with no structure is the fastest path to notes nobody reads. How to Structure Meeting Notes During the Meeting During a meeting, speed and clarity matter more than perfection. Your job is to capture enough structure in real time so the notes are usable the moment the meeting ends. Here are the core habits that make in-meeting note-taking work: Write decisions as they happen, not during the recap. By the time someone summarizes, key context has already been lost. Capture action items with three pieces of information: what needs to happen, who owns it, and when it’s due. Use shorthand for speed, but keep it consistent so your notes translate cleanly when you revisit them after. Note any open questions or unresolved items separately so they don’t get buried in the main discussion thread. Note-Taking Methods and Frameworks There are several frameworks worth knowing before you pick one for your team. The Cornell Method Divide your page into three zones: a narrow left column for cues and questions, a wide right column for notes taken during the meeting, and a summary section at the bottom. It works well for information-dense sessions where you need to review and synthesize afterward. Cornell University’s Learning Strategies Center has a full breakdown of the system. The Outline Method Use hierarchical indentation to capture main topics, subtopics, and supporting details. Most people default to this structure because it maps naturally onto agenda items. The Mapping Method Draw a visual web with the central topic at the center and branches for related ideas. Useful for brainstorming sessions where discussion is non-linear. Method Format Best For When to Use It Cornell Narrow left cue column, wide right notes column, summary section at the bottom Information-dense sessions that need review and synthesis afterward Structured workshops, training sessions, complex briefings Outline Hierarchical indentation by topic, subtopic, and detail Agenda-driven meetings with a clear topic order Most standard team meetings, project syncs, standups Mapping Visual web with a central topic and branches for related ideas Non-linear discussions where ideas build on each other freely Strategy sessions, ideation meetings, open-ended brainstorming Choosing a Framework No single method fits every meeting type. A structured agenda meeting suits the outline method; a strategy session with open discussion may benefit from mapping. The right choice depends on your meeting format, how decisions get made, and how notes will be distributed afterward. How to Write Meeting Minutes as a Secretary As a secretary, your job is to create a clear, accurate record. Learning how to take minutes in a meeting properly means the whole group can reference it later, including everyone on the team and not merely the person who wrote it down. What to Include The meeting date, time, location, and names of attendees and absentees A brief summary of each agenda item discussed, not a verbatim transcript All decisions made, including who proposed them and whether they passed Action items with a clear owner and deadline for each Any motions, votes, and their outcomes Format Tips for First-Timers Write in past tense and third person (“The team agreed…” not “We decided…”). Keep descriptions concise: one to three sentences per agenda item is usually enough. Circulate a draft within 24 hours while details are still fresh, and get approval from the meeting chair before distributing the final version. Meeting Notes Templates and Samples A well-structured template saves time and keeps records consistent across meetings. Below are the core formats worth knowing, from formal minutes to lightweight action-focused notes. Formal Meeting Minutes Template Use this for board meetings, official committee sessions, or any meeting where a legal or institutional record is required. Lightweight Meeting Notes Template For standups, syncs, and working sessions where speed matters more than formality. Date, attendees, and meeting purpose at the top Key discussion points grouped by topic Decisions made, with enough context to be understood later Action items with a named owner and deadline for each Any open questions or blockers to carry forward How to Organize and Distribute Meeting Notes After the Meeting Good meeting notes lose their value fast if they sit in a shared doc nobody revisits. Distribution and organization matter as much as the notes themselves. Send notes within 24 hours while context is fresh. Include a clear subject line, a brief summary, the full notes, and a list of action items with owners and due dates. Slack’s guide on effective meeting notes distribution covers how to structure that share-out for team alignment. For storage, pick one location and stick to it: Project management tools (Jira, Linear, Asana) keep action items tied directly to work Shared docs (Google Docs, Notion, Confluence) work well for searchable archives Team channels (Slack, Teams) are good for visibility but poor for long-term retrieval Tag notes by team, project, and date so they stay findable weeks later. How to Take Meeting Notes in Microsoft Teams Teams gives you two built-in options for capturing meeting notes: the native Notes tab inside a meeting and Copilot-generated summaries if your organization has a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. For a full walkthrough, see how to record a Teams meeting . Native Teams Meeting Notes Open any Teams meeting, select the Notes tab, and start typing. Notes sync across all attendees in real time and stay attached to the meeting event in your calendar. No setup required, no extra license needed. Copilot-Generated Summaries With a Copilot license, Teams can generate a summary, list action items, and answer follow-up questions from the transcript after the meeting ends (as of July 2026). To turn it on, go to your Teams admin center, confirm transcription is active for your organization, and Copilot will surface automatically in eligible meetings. Taking Meeting Notes with AI The best tools for AI meeting notes generally follow the same sequence: a bot joins your call, captures audio and transcript throughout, and delivers a structured summary when the meeting ends, routing decisions and action items with named owners directly into your team’s tools. Most extract action items, surface decisions, and identify speakers by name. When selecting one for your team, a few things are worth checking: Transcription accuracy across your actual languages and accents, beyond clean English audio from a single speaker Whether participant consent and notification are built into the recording flow, visible to everyone in the meeting Where your data is stored after the call ends, who has access, and how long it’s retained Whether outputs route automatically into your existing tools or require manual re-entry One limitation that catches teams off guard: AI-generated notes still need a human pass before they go out. Proper nouns get mangled, technical terms get misread, and overlapping speakers cause misattribution. A two-minute review to confirm action item owners and catch garbled decisions is worth doing every time. Automated meeting minutes cut that review burden by handling the volume work first. How to Convert Meeting Notes into Action Items and Next Steps After every meeting, do one dedicated pass through your raw notes. Scan for every commitment made out loud, then sort what you find into three categories: Decisions: already settled, recorded clearly so everyone references the same resolution later. Action items: a task with a named owner and a deadline, ready to route directly into your PM tool. Converting meeting transcripts to Jira tickets is one way to close that loop automatically. Open questions: unresolved items where you assign an owner to find the answer or carry them to the next agenda. The routing step is where follow-through breaks down. An action item that stays inside a notes doc has no accountability mechanism. Automatically creating action items from meeting transcripts gives each task a ticket, a status, and visibility. A five-minute weekly sweep keeps the list current. How Meeting Notes Get Captured, Structured, and Routed Across an Organization Spinach AI is an enterprise conversation intelligence system, the record of conversation data. Where individual AI notetakers solve one person’s problem, Spinach is deployed company-wide across Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Slack Huddles, and Webex to capture, centralize, and govern every conversation the organization has. During the meeting, Spinach captures decisions and action items with named owners; when the meeting ends, it routes structured output directly into your team’s tools, such as Jira, Linear, Slack, CRM, and more, so nothing needs to be re-keyed by hand. For organizations running meetings across multiple teams, that consistency matters. One deployment covers every call, every department, with the same governed structure and enforced policy each time, eliminating the shadow IT sprawl that comes from every team using a different personal notetaker. Final Thoughts on How to Write Meeting Notes That Actually Work Structured notes don’t need to be long or formal. They need a decision, an owner, and a deadline on every item that matters. Get those three things right and your meetings will stop repeating themselves. If you want to eliminate the manual work entirely, Spinach AI is the enterprise conversation intelligence system organizations deploy company-wide, capturing decisions and action items with named owners across every Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Slack Huddles, and Webex call, and routing structured output to your team’s tools when the meeting ends. What is the difference between meeting notes and meeting minutes? Meeting notes are informal records you shape to fit the conversation: no required format, no legal standing. Meeting minutes are formal documents used for board meetings, governance sessions, or legal proceedings, written in past tense and third person by a designated secretary, and often carrying official institutional weight. If you’re running a team standup or project sync, notes work fine; if a decision needs to be defensible on record, minutes are the right format. How should you structure meeting notes so action items actually get completed? Capture action items with three pieces of information during the meeting: what needs to happen, who owns it, and when it’s due. Someone will follow up is not an action item. How should you structure meeting notes so action items actually get completed? Capture action items with three pieces of information during the meeting: what needs to happen, who owns it, and when it’s due. “Someone will follow up” is not an action item. “Maya will send the revised Q3 budget to the team by Thursday” is. Once the meeting ends, move those items directly into your project management tool (Jira, Linear, Asana) so they have a ticket, a status, and visibility. An action item that stays inside a notes doc has no accountability mechanism. Meeting notes in Microsoft Teams: native Notes tab vs. Copilot vs. a dedicated AI tool like Spinach AI. Which should I use? The native Teams Notes tab requires no license and syncs across attendees in real time, making it fine for lightweight capture. Copilot generates post-meeting summaries and action item lists if your organization has a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, but outputs stay inside the Microsoft ecosystem and require manual re-entry into other tools. Spinach AI joins Teams meetings alongside Meet, Zoom, and Webex, captures decisions and action items with named owners during the call, and routes structured output directly into Jira, Linear, Slack, or your CRM when the meeting ends, so nothing needs to be re-keyed by hand. What’s the best way to take meeting notes electronically when AI tools still make errors? AI note-taking tools follow the same sequence: a bot joins the call, captures audio and transcript, and delivers a structured summary at meeting end. The gap most teams hit is that proper nouns get mangled, technical terms get misread, and overlapping speakers cause misattribution. A two-minute review pass to confirm action item owners and catch garbled decisions is worth doing every time before notes go out. AI handles the volume work; you handle the verification. How do you write meeting minutes as a secretary for the first time? Write in past tense and third person (“The team agreed…” not “We decided…”), keep each agenda item to one to three sentences, and record every decision with the name of who proposed it and whether it passed. Circulate a draft within 24 hours while details are still fresh, and get approval from the meeting chair before sending the final version. The most common first-timer mistake is trying to capture everything verbatim. Your job is an accurate, scannable record, not a transcript. What is taking notes in a meeting called, and does the term change based on the meeting type? The person capturing notes is typically called a note-taker, minute-taker, or recording secretary, depending on the formality of the meeting. In governance or board contexts, the role is usually called secretary, and the output is called minutes; in working team sessions, the output is simply called meeting notes. The term matters because it signals the expected format, level of detail, and whether the record carries institutional weight. What should post meeting notes include that you might skip during the meeting itself? Post meeting notes should include a clean list of action items with named owners and deadlines, any decisions that were made with enough context to be understood weeks later, and open questions that were parked for a future meeting. During the meeting you often capture shorthand; the post-meeting pass is where you translate that into a record someone else can act on without needing to ask you what it means. Meeting notes vs minutes: which format should a first-time secretary use for a school meeting? For school committee or board meetings, formal minutes are the right format because they serve as an official record of decisions, votes, and attendance. Write in past tense and third person, record each agenda item in one to three sentences, and capture every motion and its outcome. For informal staff or team meetings at school, lightweight notes with decisions and action items are fine and faster to produce. What is a simple minutes of meeting sample structure I can reuse across most meetings? A simple, reusable structure has five sections: header (meeting title, date, time, location), attendees (names and any absentees), agenda items covered (one to three sentences each), decisions and action items (with named owner and due date for each task), and next steps (next meeting date and any open questions carried forward). This structure works for most team syncs and committee sessions without modification. Is there a meeting minutes synonym I should know, and does the word choice affect how notes are received? Common synonyms include meeting record, minutes of meeting, official record, and board record — all refer to the same formal document. The word choice does signal expectations: calling something minutes tells recipients it is a formal, reviewable record, while calling it notes signals flexibility. In regulated or governance contexts, use minutes to set the right expectation about the document’s standing. What is the correct meeting minutes pronunciation, and why do people say ‘minutes’ instead of ‘time’? It is pronounced exactly like the unit of time — MIN-its — and the word shares that same Latin root, minuta, meaning small or detailed. In this context it refers to small details written down, not a measure of sixty seconds. The confusion is common because the two meanings are spelled and pronounced identically, but context always makes clear which one is intended. How do you take meeting notes with AI when your team uses multiple meeting platforms like Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet? The cleanest approach is a single AI tool that works across all your platforms rather than a separate note-taker per product. Spinach AI joins meetings across Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Slack Huddles, and Webex, so the same governed structure and output routing applies regardless of which platform a given team uses. That consistency matters at scale because different tools per team produce shadow IT and no shared organizational record. Should I use a Cornell, outline, or mapping method for structuring meeting notes in a fast-moving sprint planning session? The outline method works best for sprint planning because the meeting follows a clear agenda order — backlog items, priorities, assignments — which maps naturally onto hierarchical indentation. Cornell is better suited to dense information sessions where you need to review and synthesize later. Mapping is for non-linear brainstorming where ideas build on each other freely, which is rarely the shape of a sprint planning session. How do you generate meeting notes in Microsoft Teams using Copilot, and what are the limits of that approach? With a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, go to your Teams admin center, confirm transcription is active for your organization, and Copilot will surface automatically in eligible meetings to generate a summary and action item list after the meeting ends. The main limit is that outputs stay inside the Microsoft ecosystem, so decisions and action items require manual re-entry into Jira, Linear, Slack, or any CRM your team uses — there is no automatic routing into external tools. What is the best way to take meeting notes electronically when you want action items to automatically become trackable tasks? Route action items directly into your project management tool at the moment you capture them, rather than leaving them inside a notes document. Tools like Jira, Linear, and Asana give each task a ticket, a status, and visibility — an action item that stays in a shared doc has no accountability mechanism. If you want the routing to happen without manual re-entry, an AI meeting assistant that integrates natively with your PM tools can move decisions and named-owner action items into tickets as soon as the meeting ends. Second Quarter net loss of $241.4 million compared to net loss of $29.0 million in the first quarter of 2026, primarily driven by a $176.3 million debt extinguishment charge related to the refinancing of our senior secured notes due 2028 and 2030 and convertible bonds due 2028. Second Quarter Adjusted EBITDA of $43.8 million, a decrease of $44.7 million or 51% compared to the first quarter of 2026. Refinanced substantially all existing debt through the issuance of senior secured notes due 2032 and 2034 and convertible notes due 2033, extending debt maturities and reducing financing costs. Amended super senior revolving credit facility, increasing the commitments to $250.0 million, reducing the margin, extending the maturity date, and further strengthening liquidity. Subsequent to quarter end, completed the acquisition of five premium jack-up rigs via new 50/50 joint venture for a total purchase price of $287 million. Year-to-date 2026, the Company has been awarded 21 contract commitments, representing approximately 4,350 days and $541 million of Dayrate Equivalent Backlog. Chief Executive Officer Bruno Morand commented: "Our operational performance in the second quarter of 2026 resulted in technical utilization of 98.4% and economic utilization of 96.4%. Revenue for the period was $232.3 million, as the average number of rigs operating declined from 22.4 in Q1 to 21.2 in Q2. Second Quarter Adjusted EBITDA was $43.8 million, a decline of $44.7 million compared with Q1. The sequential decrease was primarily driven by four factors. First, we incurred additional preparation work and regulatory approval activities for the Odin ahead of its contract in the U.S., with $22.5 million of operating expenses during the quarter, a $11.1 million quarter-on-quarter increase. Second, six rigs were transitioning between contracts during the quarter, leading to reduced revenue; however, this impact is now largely behind us as these rigs have now commenced their contracts. Third, the conflict in the Middle East drove incrementally higher insurance and fuel costs, with fuel costs also impacted by the rigs transitioning contracts, which together resulted in a $7.3 million quarter-on-quarter increase in rig operating expenses. Finally, we also recognized $10.8 million of credit losses related to a former customer in West Africa, an increase of $4.8 million compared to the prior quarter. Following this additional provision, we carry no net receivables from this customer on our balance sheet. Contract preparation for the Odin took longer than anticipated with regulatory approvals received in mid-July. In light of operating constraints during the hurricane season, we agreed with our customers to revise the rig’s deployment sequence to improve overall operating efficiency. The Odin is currently preparing to mobilize to its first location, where it will commence the previously announced two-well firm contract with an undisclosed customer. Upon completion of this contract, the rig is expected to transition directly to Cantium. We are disappointed with the delays for the Odin, and the initial start-up requirements were greater than we would typically expect when entering a new market. This resulted in higher cost and delays in revenue. The elevated rig transition activity experienced during Q2 is now substantially complete. The Idun, Gunnlod, Skald, Sif, Natt and Prospector 5, which were transitioning into or between contracts during the quarter, are now fully operational. Together with the commencement of the Odin contract, we expect to average approximately 23 active rigs during Q3. Based on this projected activity level, we expect Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 to improve significantly from the second quarter. Since the last earnings report, we have secured eight contract commitments, representing over 2,100 days of additional firm work. 2026 contract coverage is now at 73% at an average dayrate of approximately $134,000 per day with coverage in the second half of the year of 70%. During the quarter, we successfully refinanced substantially all of our debt through the issuance of $300 million of convertible notes and $2,035 million of senior secured notes, while also upsizing our super senior RCF to $250 million. These transactions extended our maturities, reduced financing costs, and further strengthened our liquidity. Subsequent to quarter end, our 50/50 joint venture with our long-term Mexican well construction partner completed the purchase of five premium jack-ups from Fontis at an attractive valuation and with limited equity committed. Currently, three of these rigs are contracted, with two of them operating and the third expected to commence operations later in Q3 2026. Our focus now is deploying the remaining rigs and converting the opportunity pipeline into contracted work. In closing, the Middle East conflict has reduced near-term visibility, delaying tenders, contract start dates, and the region’s recovery. This uncertainty is also affecting several other offshore markets, though not all, making it difficult to provide a crisp outlook for our activity. What is clear, however, is that the prolonged disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has driven global inventories to exceptionally low levels. Rebuilding those inventories, even under a moderate demand outlook, will require sustained production drilling, both onshore and offshore. We therefore expect the market to strengthen as stability returns. Our priorities are clear: deploy our expanded premium jack-up fleet, use its scale and quality to navigate changing market conditions, and deliver value to shareholders as the cycle improves.” Conference Call: A conference call and webcast are scheduled for 09:00 New York time (15:00 CEST) on Wednesday, August 12, 2026. title: Perspectives in Aseptic Manufacturing: Establishing a Container Closure System - Engineering for Integrity
summary: Learn how container closure systems maintain sterility, closure integrity, and fill finish performance in aseptic manufacturing and sterile packaging.
body_text: Eric Kurtz Manager Technical Product Development August 04, 2026 Perspectives in Aseptic Manufacturing: Establishing a Container Closure System - Engineering for Integrity A container closure system(CCS) is an engineered solution to protect drug product. It must maintain sterility, support container closure integrity, and perform consistently within automated fill/finish operations. And a comprehensive CCS strategy integrates materials science, equipment compatibility, contamination control, and scalability. Washed and sterilized bulk vials coming out of a depyrogenation tunnel and accumulating on a rotary table prior to filling. Image courtesy of Optima Packaging Group GmbH. Used with permission. Establishing a robust CCS requires more than selecting a vial and stopper. Elastomeric closures must withstand mechanical interaction with feeding systems, pick‑and‑place equipment, and plunger insertion mechanisms without compromising sealing performance. Surface damage, abrasion, or incompatibility with vent tubes can negatively affect integrity, particularly for laminated designs. Barrier configuration also plays a role. Whether operating within a Restricted Access Barrier Systems (RABS) or isolator system, contamination control strategies must demonstrate effective risk management. Closed isolator systems can reduce human intervention and strengthen environmental control. RABS configurations remain viable when supported by appropriate procedural and engineering controls. In both cases, the container closure system must be compatible with the selected barrier approach. Component format influences performance and flexibility. The industry continues to migrate toward ready‑to‑use formats for vials, syringes, and cartridges. Ready-to-use (RTU) components reduce washing and sterilization requirements, lower contamination risk, and support flexible manufacturing models. Nested configurations further affect transport mechanisms, closure introduction, and line design. Plunger placement strategy is another critical consideration. Vacuum‑assisted insertion, vent tube selection, and headspace modeling influence residual bubble size and internal pressure equilibrium. These variables must be evaluated to avoid contaminant ingress or unintended product migration. West approaches these considerations holistically, partnering with customers to align integrity, machinability, and lifecycle performance from early development through commercial production. If you are evaluating or refining your CCS, our technical teams are ready to support your assessment. Click here to Contact Us . title: ChatGPT Work and Codex Education Plugins Launch for K-12
summary: OpenAI launches education plugins for ChatGPT Work and Codex, enabling K-12 teachers, college educators, and students to learn, teach, and build with AI tools.
body_text: OpenAI has introduced a suite of education-focused plugins for ChatGPT Work and Codex, designed to support K-12 teachers, college educators, and students across learning, teaching, research, and development activities. The launch marks a significant expansion of AI capabilities into formal education environments, providing structured tools that address specific classroom and academic needs. Core Education Plugin Features The new plugins integrate directly into ChatGPT Work and Codex, offering educators specialized functionality for lesson planning, curriculum development, and student assessment. Teachers can generate customized learning materials, create differentiated instruction resources, and develop assessment rubrics aligned to specific educational standards. The tools support multiple subject areas and grade levels, allowing for adaptation across diverse classroom contexts. For students, the plugins provide research assistance, coding tutorials through Codex, and interactive learning experiences. The system maintains context across sessions, enabling ongoing projects and iterative learning processes. College educators gain access to advanced research tools, citation management, and collaborative features that support both synchronous and asynchronous teaching models. K-12 Classroom Applications Primary and secondary educators can leverage the plugins to address common classroom challenges: Automated generation of differentiated worksheets and activities for mixed-ability classrooms Real-time feedback on student writing and coding assignments Creation of visual aids, diagrams, and explanatory content for complex concepts Development of project-based learning frameworks with scaffolding support The tools include safety features and content filtering appropriate for younger students, with administrative controls that allow school districts to customize access levels and usage parameters. Codex Integration for Computer Science Education The Codex component specifically targets programming education, offering students and teachers interactive coding environments with intelligent assistance. Students can receive step-by-step guidance on debugging, explanations of programming concepts in natural language, and example code that illustrates best practices. Teachers gain curriculum templates for introductory through advanced computer science courses, complete with auto-graded assignments and progress tracking. The integration supports multiple programming languages and frameworks, making it applicable to web development, data science, and software engineering courses at both high school and university levels. Research and Collaboration Tools College-level educators and graduate students benefit from enhanced research capabilities built into the plugins. Features include literature review assistance, hypothesis generation, experimental design suggestions, and data analysis support. The tools can process academic papers, extract key findings, and synthesize information across multiple sources while maintaining proper attribution. Collaborative features enable group projects, peer review workflows, and shared resource libraries. Educators can create team workspaces where students collaborate on research papers, coding projects, or multimedia presentations with AI-assisted guidance throughout the process. What This Means OpenAI's education plugins represent a deliberate effort to bring structured AI assistance into formal learning environments. By providing tools specifically designed for educational workflows rather than general-purpose chatbots, the company addresses concerns about appropriate AI use in classrooms while empowering educators to enhance instruction quality. The launch positions ChatGPT Work and Codex as comprehensive platforms for educational institutions seeking to integrate AI capabilities systematically. As adoption grows, these tools may influence pedagogical approaches across K-12 and higher education, shifting focus toward AI-augmented instruction models that prioritize critical thinking and creative application over rote learning.

title: Disney Legends in Conversation: Jerry Bruckheimer
summary: Jerry Bruckheimer is a film and television producer behind Disney franchises such as 'Pirates of the Caribbean' and 'National Treasure.'
body_text: Disney Legends in Conversation: Jerry Bruckheimer Entertainment August 10, 2026 5 min. read The Disney Legends Award ceremony will mark the final day of D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event presented by Visa® , a one-of-a-kind, multi-day fan experience showcasing the very best in creative storytelling and innovation from across the worlds of Disney. Hosted by Ryan Seacrest , the event will be filled with tributes and unforgettable moments to honor and celebrate the icons behind the magic who have made a lasting impact on Disney. This year, The Walt Disney Company’s highest honor will be presented to 13 individuals — Chris Berman , Jerry Bruckheimer , Susan Egan , Eric Goldberg , Anne Hathaway , Bob Iger , Kim Irvine , Dwayne Johnson , the Jonas Brothers , Lin‑Manuel Miranda , and Alan Tudyk — who for generations have defined Disney across entertainment, storytelling, and experiences. In an exclusive Q&A, Jerry Bruckheimer —who is being recognized in the Film category—reflects on his contributions to the company and what it means to be named a Disney Legend. How does it feel to be honored as a Disney Legend? It’s amazing. Given the long history of Disney — and my relationship with it — and the kind of entertainment they have made for so many decades, it’s really quite the honor. What Disney films inspired you to become a film producer? Boy, it’s hard to say. Some of the pirate movies, like Treasure Island — I really loved those as a kid. They had great characters and great themes, and it was real family entertainment. And that’s what I aspire to do with the movies I make. Pirates of the Caribbean is one of the most successful film franchises of all time. What do you remember about making The Curse of the Black Pearl , and how does that compare to your experience producing the fifth movie, Dead Men Tell No Tales ? The first one, we had no idea [it would be such a hit]. The conventional wisdom at the time was, “How can you make a movie about a theme park ride?” The media was really down on the film before they saw it — and they were shocked when they saw how inventive it was, how funny it was, and how Disney moved into a whole other arena by making that movie. It was [fellow Disney Legend and former CEO of The Walt Disney Company] Bob Iger who greenlit that film, so it’s thanks to him we got the movie made. And what you created onscreen was integrated into the attraction years later. It sure is great when you see the Captain Jack Sparrow Audio-Animatronic® [figure]. And it’s really a thrill that we can entertain kids for many generations moving forward. Why do you think the Pirates films have resonated so deeply with fans? They have compelling characters and humor. They’re a little scary. There’s romance. And, the fact is, there’s also an irreverent pirate — who, it turns out, has a good heart. In addition to Pirates of the Caribbean , you’ve produced a slew of blockbusters for Disney, from Armageddon and Remember the Titans to Pearl Harbor and National Treasure . What has made your partnership with Disney work so well over the years? It’s a great group, and the various managements I’ve worked with over the years have shepherded me into making really good movies. And the way Disney markets and distributes their films, they’re the best. I have to say, I’m proud of all those movies. They’re all your kids, so I can’t pick a favorite. If there is one — at least in the Disney group — it’s the Pirates franchise that has entertained audiences for quite a few years. Swashbuckling Adventure Watch Now The roguish yet charming Captain Jack Sparrow’s idyllic pirate life capsizes after his nemesis, the wily Captain Barbossa, steals his ship and attacks the town of Port Royal, kidnapping the governor’s daughter, Elizabeth. In a gallant attempt to rescue her and recapture the ship, Elizabeth’s childhood friend Will Turner joins forces with Jack. What Will doesn’t know is that a cursed treasure has doomed Barbossa and his crew to live forever as the undead. 2003 Streaming on Disney+ Your productions are known for combining heart with scale. Why do you think Disney characters and worlds lend themselves so well to the stories you like to tell? They’re four-quadrant films. I love to be able to entertain full audiences, and that’s what Disney does. It’s universal storytelling, and fortunately for me, the movies I make fit into that basket. About the Disney Legends Program The Disney Legends Awards program is a 39-year tradition of The Walt Disney Company, which began when Fred MacMurray was honored in 1987. Including this year’s honorees, a total of 329 Disney Legends has been named. Past Disney Legends include Tim Allen , Julie Andrews , Angela Bassett , Tony Baxter , Kristen Bell , James Cameron , Jamie Lee Curtis , Miley Cyrus , Marc Davis , Robert Downey Jr. , Harrison Ford , Annette Funicello , Josh Gad , Whoopi Goldberg , Jonathan Groff , Steve Jobs , Elton John , Angela Lansbury , Stan Lee , George Lucas , Steve Martin , Burny Mattinson , Alan Menken , Idina Menzel , Hayley Mills , Fess Parker , Ellen Pompeo , Robin Roberts , the Sherman Brothers , Marty Sklar , Dick Van Dyke , Barbara Walters , Betty White , John Williams , Robin Williams , and Oprah Winfrey . title: Announcing our $17.5M Series A led by Base10
summary: Axle announces itʼs $17.5M Series A to continue building the AI native clearinghouse for insurance
body_text: Axle announces its $17.5M Series A to continue building the AI native clearinghouse for insurance Announcing our $17.5M Series A led by Base10 We're thrilled to announce $17.5M in Series A funding led by Base10 Partners , with continued investment from Y Combinator, and Gradient Ventures ; and participation from Stage2 Capital , Chris Bayley (Co-Founder and CEO of Cover Genius), and other industry angel investors. They join our existing investors, including the early team at Plaid. Over the last six months, we've tripled the number of workflows we automate. We now clear more than $100B in coverage every year for over 4,000 businesses - mortgage lenders, auto dealers, rental car companies, auto lenders, employers, and more - including dozens of Fortune 500 companies like Rocket Mortgage, Avis, Experian, and Sonic Automotive. Along the way, we've sped those workflows up by 20x and recovered hundreds of millions of dollars in losses for our customers. "Before Axle, verifying a renter's insurance meant either absorbing the risk or slowing the customer down at the counter. Axle gives us an instant, accurate answer at the moment it matters, and it has helped us recover millions in losses we used to write off each year." - Jordan Bannantine, Head of Risk Management at SIXT An $8.3 trillion industry still running on paper and phone calls Insurance is the $8.3 trillion backbone of the economy. You need it to close a mortgage, buy a car, lease an apartment, rent a vehicle, drive for work, move furniture… the list goes on and on. And yet, the businesses that depend on it still run on fax machines and phone calls to verify, update, and monitor policies. ‍ For example, a single mortgage can require a lender to engage with insurance more than 10 times over the life of a loan: from calculating DTI, to ensuring proper coverage, selling the loan to Fannie Mae, paying your escrow bill every year, and supporting you if something ever happens. ‍ The reason is structural. Unlike banking and credit, insurance has never had a common ledger. A single large carrier can run 15 or more separate policy systems, and much of the data still lives in unstructured documents built for brokers, not software. Building the clearinghouse for insurance That's where Axle comes in. Our infrastructure and AI agents integrate into those fragmented systems, route each request to the right place, and normalize messy, unstructured data into a single standard. The result is one clean API that software and AI agents can build on to automate the workflows that the economy runs on: Does my customer have insurance? Does it meet my requirements? Can you update changes to the policy? Has anything changed? "In 2026, no one should be faxing PDFs or sitting on hold to confirm a policy. Few real economy industries are more foundational, or more manual, than insurance. The Axle team built the rails that make insurance programmable, and we believe a generation of products will be built on top of them." - Adeyemi Ajao, Co-founder and Managing Partner at Base10 Partners Whatʼs Next? Having proven the model across five distinct markets, we'll use the funding from this round to scale our hiring across engineering and go-to-market teams, and to expand the clearinghouse to more than 50 segments spanning Home, Auto, Renters, Commercial, and Specialty insurance, while deepening our direct relationships with carriers who increasingly use Axle as a governed gateway to the businesses and consumers they serve. But thatʼs just the start: everything the economy runs on - credit, payments, identity, income - has a clearinghouse in the middle. Insurance never has. We're building it. Once insurance is standardized and programmable, it becomes far more valuable to the carriers who write it, the businesses that rely on it, and the hundreds of millions of consumers it protects. Come build with us We're hiring. We're growing the team across product, engineering, and go-to-market, and we'd love to meet people who want to work on foundational infrastructure for a multi-trillion-dollar industry. See our open roles on our job board . Weʼre partnering. If your business depends on insurance, we'd love to show you what instant verification, monitoring, and policy updates can do for your workflows. Or, if you're a carrier looking to make your policies programmable through a governed gateway, we'd love to talk. Reach out here . To see the latest from team Axle, follow us on LinkedIn ! Thank you To our customers - the 4,000+ real-economy businesses that trust Axle to automate mission-critical workflows that the economy runs on. We would not get to do this without you. Every time we hear a story of how Axle prevented a loss from happening, a bad actor from making an adverse action, or even helping an end consumer realize they had the wrong VIN on their policy, weʼre reminded of why we do this. To our team - thank you for building infrastructure that clears more than $100B in coverage every year and pushing the frontier of what it means to be accurate, reliable, and easy to use.
